This incident follows previous legal troubles involving alcohol, for which LaBeouf was ordered to seek treatment by a judge last year. Representatives for LaBeouf have not commented on the latest arrest.

597958_597958.caption: Searches for two separate racist slurs pinpoint the home of the US president Barack Obama the White House
597958_597958.article_context: The article profiles several popular parody Twitter accounts in the UK, highlighting the creators behind each one and their motivations. These accounts include @CherylKerl, a comedic Geordie version of Cheryl Cole; @chilean_miner, which imagined the lives of trapped Chilean miners with light-hearted tweets; @CatBinLady, a satirical character inspired by a viral news story; @DrSamuelJohnson, a playful take on the 18th-century lexicographer; and @dianainheaven, which humorously depicts Princess Diana tweeting from the afterlife. Each account rapidly gained thousands of followers and media attention, showing how humour and clever character creation can drive success on social media.

1648241_1648241.caption: The event was picked up in April 2009 by Nasa s Swift telescope
1648241_1648241.article_context: NASA's Swift space observatory detected a gamma-ray burst, designated GRB 090429B, which is considered the most distant single astronomical event ever observed and likely originated from the collapse of a giant star just 520 million years after the Big Bang. The light from this explosion traveled about 13.14 billion years to reach Earth, providing valuable insight into the early Universe and the formation of its first stars and galaxies. While there is some uncertainty in such measurements, scientists are eager to study these distant phenomena to better understand cosmic evolution during the epoch of re-ionization. The Swift mission remains crucial for discovering more early-universe events by detecting brief but powerful gamma-ray bursts.

1562874_1562874.caption: Baroness Morgan of Ely accused the UK government of high handed arrogance
1562874_1562874.article_context: The UK government faces calls to abandon plans to restrict public sector strikes in Wales after a leaked letter revealed ministers privately acknowledge they have a 'very weak case' for imposing such measures on devolved services. Critics, including Welsh ministers and Labour politicians, argue the Trade Union Bill infringes on devolved powers over areas like health and education. The Welsh government has threatened legal action if Westminster proceeds. Despite this, the UK government says it remains committed to the bill, which would require 40% support from eligible voters for strike action in key services.

77097_77097.caption: Protesters ransack the Muslim Brotherhood headquarters in the Muqattam district in Cairo Because the Islamist group backed Morsi protesters took out their frustrations with the group
77097_77097.article_context: Egypt’s interim president Adly Mansour swore in a new 34-member cabinet led by interim Prime Minister Hazem el-Beblawi, following the military ouster of President Mohamed Morsi. The new cabinet is composed mainly of liberals and technocrats, with no representatives from Islamist parties including the Muslim Brotherhood and the ultra-conservative Nour party, both of which declined to participate. The formation of the new government comes amid ongoing unrest, with violent clashes between security forces and Morsi supporters resulting in multiple deaths and injuries, and mass arrests of protesters. The visit of U.S. Deputy Secretary of State William J. Burns signaled U.S. support for Egypt’s interim leaders, though skepticism remains among various Egyptian factions.

151688_151688.caption: Fighters from the Free Syrian Army take part in a battle against Islamic State jihadists in the village of Yahmoul north of Aleppo
151688_151688.article_context: A senior United Nations official announced that the Syrian government has refused to grant permits for aid convoys to enter the besieged city of Aleppo, despite a cease-fire brokered by the United States and Russia that has reduced fighting in key areas. Forty U.N. trucks loaded with food and medical supplies remain stuck at the Syria-Turkey border, highlighting major challenges in implementing humanitarian relief under the agreement. Both the Syrian government and rebel groups have yet to withdraw from the key Castello Road, complicating efforts to open aid routes. The stalemate has led to heightened tensions between the U.S. and Russia, and cast doubt on the effectiveness of the cease-fire and future coordinated actions against extremist groups.

281981_281981.caption: A police officer bows his head during the funeral for Dallas Police senior Cpl Lorne Ahrens
281981_281981.article_context: Three police officers were killed and three others wounded in a shooting in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, when a gunman opened fire near police headquarters. The attacker, Gavin E. Long, a former Marine from Kansas City, was killed at the scene. The incident followed recent national tensions over police shootings, including the death of Alton Sterling by Baton Rouge police and an earlier attack on officers in Dallas. President Obama condemned the violence, urging unity and restraint from inflammatory rhetoric. Authorities believe Long acted alone and are investigating his possible motives and connections. The shooting prompted law enforcement agencies in other cities to implement new safety measures for officers.

1076665_1076665.caption: Greenpeace activists aboard a Shell oil rig in the Pacific
1076665_1076665.article_context: Six Greenpeace activists boarded the Polar Pioneer drill rig in the Pacific Ocean as it was being transported toward Seattle for Shell's planned Arctic offshore drilling on Alaska leases. The activists, protesting Shell's drilling operations in the Arctic, intend to unfurl a banner but do not plan to interfere with the vessel's navigation. Shell condemned the action as illegal and insisted drilling preparations would continue, while conservation groups remain strongly opposed due to environmental concerns. The incident highlights ongoing controversy around Arctic oil exploration and the risks of operations in remote, ice-choked waters.

107717_107717.caption: This vacant office building at 6116 Executive Blvd in Rockville Md is in foreclosure
107717_107717.article_context: Suburban office parks across the Washington region are becoming increasingly vacant, with millions of square feet left unused as government agencies and major companies like Marriott move operations to more urban, Metro-accessible areas. Changing work habits, such as telecommuting and a preference for walkable, city-like environments, have made these office parks less desirable, leading to drastic drops in their value and widespread abandonment. Despite some upticks in leasing for smaller buildings and efforts by tech giants to reinvent the office park concept, traditional suburban office parks now symbolize a fading way of American work life, characterized by isolation and disconnection.

179014_179014.caption: Robin Wilson leads chanting as airport workers and supporters rally for better wages at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Arlington
179014_179014.article_context: Airport workers at Washington's Reagan National and Dulles International have joined a national campaign for a $15-an-hour minimum wage and better benefits, highlighting extremely low pay and poor working conditions. Many of these workers, mostly immigrants and minorities, currently earn as little as $6.75 per hour and often work multiple jobs to support their families. The campaign, organized by the 32BJ Service Employees International Union, reflects broader struggles at airports nationwide, where outsourcing has resulted in declining wages and reduced job security. Previous actions at other airports have led to wage increases and expanded benefits, and Washington-area workers are prepared to escalate their advocacy if needed.

441925_441925.caption: Climate Camp cyclists leaving Waterloo for Blackheath
441925_441925.article_context: This year's Climate Camp protest at Blackheath, south-east London, saw a significant involvement of cyclists, with about 150 activists arriving by bike as part of a coordinated 'swoop' to establish the protest site. The article highlights the growing role of bicycles in environmental demonstrations and civil disobedience, pointing out their practicality for group movement, quick arrivals, and easy escapes. The trend has also prompted police to use bikes in response, illustrating the evolving dynamics of urban protest activities.

844065_844065.caption: Afghanistan s presidential candidates Abdullah Abdullah left and Ashraf Ghani shake hands at the signing of their powersharing deal
844065_844065.article_context: Ashraf Ghani has been declared Afghanistan’s new president after months of electoral crisis and accusations of fraud, resolving the deadlock through a US-brokered power-sharing agreement with his rival Abdullah Abdullah. Under the deal, Ghani will lead the cabinet and strategic functions, while Abdullah appoints a chief executive to handle day-to-day governance. The arrangement leaves questions about its effectiveness and legitimacy but offers a path forward for addressing urgent issues such as signing a critical security pact with the US, tackling economic instability, restoring donor trust, and potentially opening talks with the Taliban.

162744_162744.caption: Google removes game simulating Gaza attacks
162744_162744.article_context: Two smartphone games depicting the ongoing Gaza conflict, Bomb Gaza and Gaza Assault: Code Red, were widely criticized for their insensitive and reductionist portrayal of violence, leading to their removal from Google’s app store. While many other video games have 'gamified' real-world war zones, the immediacy and divisiveness of the Gaza conflict set these titles apart and sparked public backlash. The article discusses whether video games about contemporary conflicts can have merit, citing academic perspectives that such games may help players understand moral complexities and foster empathy, as with projects like PeaceMaker. The piece concludes by suggesting that while some war games may be offensive, others could contribute positively to public understanding of conflicts.

927413_927413.caption: Obama who is seen as the first president to use the internet to campaign warned university students against being distracted by Xboxes iPods and other technology
927413_927413.article_context: President Barack Obama, speaking at Hampton University's commencement, warned graduates about the dangers of relying too much on modern technology for information, highlighting how devices like iPods and Xboxes can become distractions rather than tools for empowerment. Despite his own successful use of social media in the 2008 election, Obama emphasized the importance of education to navigate today’s challenging economic climate, ongoing wars, and a fast-paced media environment. He called on graduates, particularly black students, to serve as role models and mentors, underscoring that education is crucial for discerning truth amid widespread misinformation.

1545832_1545832.caption: An Israeli woman surveys a building damaged by Palestinian mortar fire
1545832_1545832.article_context: An Israeli airstrike in Gaza killed three senior Hamas military commanders, including Raed al-Attar, Mohammed Abu Shamala, and Mohammed Barhoum, in an attack that left at least 10 dead. The strike followed the collapse of ceasefire talks, reigniting hostilities with rocket fire on Israel and retaliatory airstrikes. Israel praised its intelligence services and vowed to continue operations until security goals are met, while Hamas condemned the killings and abandoned negotiations for a long-term truce. The UN Security Council expressed concern over the renewed violence, as civilian casualties in Gaza continue to rise.

907874_907874.caption: Westwood parks her armoured vehicle outside Cameron s home in Chadlington
907874_907874.article_context: Fashion designer Dame Vivienne Westwood led a protest to Prime Minister David Cameron’s home in Oxfordshire, arriving in an armored vehicle as part of a demonstration. The event attracted media attention with participants voicing their concerns, while police oversaw the situation. Westwood and her group made their stance public through symbolic gestures and posed for cameras outside Cameron’s residence.

120303_120303.caption: Displaced Iraqi children sit inside a tent at a temporary camp set up to shelter people fleeing violence in northern Iraq
120303_120303.article_context: ISIS insurgents have launched a major offensive across Iraq, seizing large territories, including key cities, airports, and military bases, and committing widespread executions that the UN says likely constitute war crimes. The escalating violence has triggered a humanitarian crisis, displacing hundreds of thousands of Iraqis and raising fears of a new civil war. The United States is deploying up to 275 military personnel to protect its embassy in Baghdad, and diplomatic discussions between the US and Iran have taken place to consider possible cooperation against ISIS. President Obama is reviewing military options, including airstrikes, as international concern grows over Iraq’s destabilization.

231969_231969.caption: Martin Shkreli CEO of Turing Pharmaceuticals is brought out of 26 Federal Plaza by law enforcement officials after being arrested for securities fraud on Dec 17 2015 in New York
231969_231969.article_context: Martin Shkreli, former CEO of Turing Pharmaceuticals, was charged with running a Ponzi scheme, misappropriating funds, and defrauding investors during his time at hedge funds and Retrophin. The SEC also filed civil charges against him. After pleading not guilty and resigning from Turing, Shkreli asserted his innocence amid heavy criticism for previous drug price hikes. The article also highlights other notable executives convicted of fraud and corporate misconduct, including Martha Stewart, Martin Grass, Bernard Ebbers, Jeffrey Skilling, and Dennis Kozlowski, underscoring a pattern of high-profile legal troubles among business leaders.

926912_926912.caption: China India and Brazil s delegates at COP21 in Le Bourget Paris Developing countries including South Africa say OECD study exaggerates money raised for poor countries
926912_926912.article_context: China, Brazil, South Africa, and India have rejected an OECD report claiming rich countries have already mobilized nearly two-thirds of the $100 billion climate finance pledged in 2009, arguing the methodology includes double-counted and loaned funds, and puts the actual figure far lower. This dispute highlights finance as a major obstacle in ongoing climate talks. Meanwhile, the EU and dozens of vulnerable countries have called for a more ambitious climate deal, further splitting the negotiating group. Debate continues over whether to set a long-term global warming limit of 2C or 1.5C, with support for the lower target strengthening among vulnerable nations and with expected backing from the Pope, whose intervention emphasizes climate change as a human rights issue.

643901_643901.caption: Amanda Knox attends court at the beginning of the Meredith Kercher murder trial
643901_643901.article_context: Amanda Knox, an American exchange student, is set to testify at her trial in Italy where she is accused of murdering her British flatmate, Meredith Kercher, in 2007. Prosecutors allege Kercher was killed during a sex game involving Knox, her Italian boyfriend Raffaele Sollecito, and Rudy Hermann Guede, who was already convicted and sentenced in a separate trial. DNA evidence is a key part of the prosecution’s case, and Knox faces life imprisonment if convicted. The trial began in January with a verdict expected after the summer break.

1034693_1034693.caption: Cameron wasn t at the table when Merkel and Hollande met Putin to discuss the Ukraine crisis
1034693_1034693.article_context: British Prime Minister David Cameron's foreign policy, once celebrated for its role in the 2011 Libya intervention, has come under intense scrutiny as Libya descends into chaos and the UK's global influence appears diminished. Critics blame both a more complex international landscape and self-inflicted wounds, such as deep UK defence cuts and uncertainty over EU membership, for Britain's waning power. Key failures include the lack of post-intervention planning in Libya, the failed Commons vote on Syria, and the UK's exclusion from key negotiations over Ukraine. While the government argues it has diversified diplomatic ties and maintained commitments to foreign aid and human rights, analysts and political opponents accuse Cameron's administration of foreign policy drift and a loss of standing in both Europe and the wider world.

124606_124606.caption: A column of combat vehicles one flying a Russian flag move through the streets near Kramatorsk
124606_124606.article_context: Ukraine's newly installed government discovered its military was severely weakened by years of corruption and neglect, leaving it unable to repel Russian troops or respond effectively to pro-Russian militants occupying eastern cities. With an empty treasury and little equipment, the Ministry of Defense launched a nationwide fundraising campaign, with citizens, businesses, and diaspora groups raising millions of dollars and donating goods to support the under-resourced army. Despite these efforts and international aid, the Ukrainian military remains undermanned and undersupplied, as Russia continues to mass troops at the border and local militants defy calls to disarm.

131211_131211.caption: A fight for the Starwood Hotel chain which Sheraton is a member of is underway following a buyout offer from a consortium led by China s Anbang Insurance Group
131211_131211.article_context: Starwood Hotels announced plans to withdraw from its $12.2 billion merger agreement with Marriott International after China's Anbang Insurance Group raised its takeover offer to $13.2 billion, calling Anbang’s bid a 'superior proposal.' This move sets the stage for a potential bidding war, with Marriott given until March 28 to respond. If successful, Anbang’s purchase would mark the largest acquisition of a U.S. company by a Chinese firm and reflects the growing trend of Chinese investments abroad amid domestic economic concerns. Starwood and Marriott have postponed shareholder votes on their deal in light of these developments.

502543_502543.caption: The megadrought in the Amazon rainforest during the summer of 2005 caused widespread damage and dieoffs to trees as depicted in this photo taken in western Amazonia in Brazil
502543_502543.article_context: NASA scientists warned that the Amazon rainforest is showing early signs of large-scale degradation linked to climate change, with an area twice the size of California suffering from an ongoing mega-drought since 2005. Satellite data revealed severe and persistent canopy damage, especially among older, larger trees, with little recovery between major droughts in 2005 and 2010. The research highlights that repeated and increasingly severe droughts are weakening the forest's resilience and may fundamentally alter its ecosystems. NASA's long-term monitoring indicates that both the quality and quantity of the Amazon rainforest are declining due to extreme climate conditions.

976828_976828.caption: US secretary of state John Kerry and UN secretarygeneral Ban Kimoon at the Paris climate talks We need to get the job done said Kerry in a hardhitting speech
976828_976828.article_context: During the final phase of critical UN climate talks in Paris, the US announced it would double its climate aid for vulnerable countries to $861 million as part of efforts to secure an ambitious global agreement. Secretary of State John Kerry emphasized the moral responsibility to support nations already facing severe climate impacts. The new pledge aims to build support among developing countries, many of whom argue that wealthy nations have not fulfilled previous funding promises. The announcement comes amid tense negotiations and ongoing skepticism from some developing countries and U.S. congressional opposition, underscoring the importance of finance in reaching a global consensus on climate action.

88074_88074.caption: Former secretary of state Hillary Clinton holds the hands of Democratic Sens Claire McCaskill
88074_88074.article_context: At the Democratic National Convention, retiring Senator Barbara Mikulski made history by officially nominating Hillary Clinton as the first female major-party presidential candidate. Mikulski, the longest-serving female senator and a trailblazer for women in politics, used her platform to celebrate Clinton's candidacy and encourage future generations of women to pursue leadership roles. Her speeches emphasized breaking political barriers and acknowledged her legacy of mentoring other women. Mikulski’s participation was widely celebrated, highlighting both her influence and the significance of Clinton’s nomination for women in American politics.

212968_212968.caption: In this Jan 3 2013 file photo an unsafe for human occupancy sticker is attached to a home that was severely damaged by Superstorm Sandy in Bay Head NJ
212968_212968.article_context: Conservative groups and budget watchdogs are opposing a $50.7 billion Superstorm Sandy aid package, arguing that much of the funding targets unrelated disasters or projects not directly connected to Sandy. In response, senior House Republicans have proposed a reduced $17 billion package focused on immediate recovery needs, while Northeast lawmakers are pushing for an amendment to add $33.7 billion, more closely matching the Senate and President Obama's $60 billion request. The House is set to vote on both versions, amidst criticism that the larger bill includes unnecessary spending and earmarks. Lawmakers remain divided over whether aid should be limited strictly to Sandy recovery or also address broader disaster mitigation and unrelated projects.

165768_165768.caption: President Obama delivers a statement on the counterISIS campaign in the Pentagon briefing room in Arlington Va on Dec 14 EPAOlivier Douliery POOL
165768_165768.article_context: Despite President Obama's initial pledge to end the Pentagon's use of supplemental 'slush fund' budgets for military operations, the controversial Overseas Contingency Operations (OCO) fund has continued throughout his presidency and is expected to persist under future administrations. The fiscal 2017 Pentagon budget includes nearly $59 billion in OCO funding for equipment purchases, European operations countering Russian aggression, and classified programs, blurring the distinction between emergency war spending and regular defense budgeting. Analysts and officials note that budget gridlock and sequestration caps have entrenched the use of OCO funds as a flexible tool to bypass budget constraints, with little progress made toward transitioning these costs into the base defense budget.

1577244_1577244.caption: Pakistan and India have overlapping territorial claims in Kashmir
1577244_1577244.article_context: Indian security forces killed at least five suspected militants in two separate gun battles in the Kashmir region, with two Indian soldiers also losing their lives. The clashes occurred in Kupwara and Sopore, reflecting ongoing violence in the disputed territory, where more than 60 militants have been killed in recent months. Despite a 2003 ceasefire between India and Pakistan, tensions and sporadic violence continue amidst unresolved territorial claims over Kashmir.

86344_86344.caption: Obama Tell GOP to raise minimum wage
86344_86344.article_context: Senate Democrats, backed by President Obama, pushed for a bill to raise the federal minimum wage, knowing it was unlikely to pass due to Republican opposition and concerns about potential job losses. The bill failed to garner enough votes, similar to other recent Democratic initiatives like the Paycheck Fairness bill. These moves are part of a strategic effort by Democrats to highlight Republican resistance to popular measures ahead of the upcoming midterm elections, aiming to sway voters by focusing on messaging rather than actual legislative success. Both parties are using such tactics to energize their bases and shape the political narrative for 2014.

947524_947524.caption: In May 2008 a 79 magnitude earthquake devastated China s main panda reserve at Wolong in Sichuan province Approximately fourfifths of the reserve was destroyed
947524_947524.article_context: Following the devastating 7.9 magnitude earthquake in Sichuan in May 2008, which destroyed most of the Wolong panda reserve, surviving pandas, including six cubs, were relocated to the Bifengxia Panda breeding centre. The earthquake killed five staff members and one panda, and over 50 pandas now reside at the temporary reserve until a new centre is built by 2015. Keepers have supported the pandas' recovery with psychological care, and in the year since the disaster, the cubs' health has improved significantly. It is estimated that only about 1,600 pandas remain in the wild.

478231_478231.caption: US legislation aimed at curbing online piracy could breach its constitution Illustration Carol and Mike WernerAlamy
478231_478231.article_context: Major media corporations have repeatedly struggled to adapt to new technologies, initially viewing innovations like audio cassettes, video recorders, DVDs, and MP3 players as threats before ultimately profiting from them. Now, these industries are backing controversial legislation in the US Congress – namely the Stop Online Piracy Act (SOPA) and the Protect IP Act (PIPA) – which aim to combat online piracy by allowing the government to block entire websites accused of copyright violations. Critics argue these bills threaten free speech, could harm innovation, and would enable broad internet censorship similar to that imposed by authoritarian regimes. There is significant opposition to the bills, but their future remains uncertain given Congressional dysfunction.

1198572_1198572.caption: Gordon Brown speaks to a resident in Cockermouth
1198572_1198572.article_context: Prime Minister Gordon Brown visited Cumbria after severe flooding caused widespread destruction, the death of a police officer, and forced many residents from their homes. Brown pledged a £1 million relief package and offered condolences, particularly praising the officer who died during the crisis. Safety inspections of bridges began as flood waters receded, revealing major damage. The Environment Agency announced an immediate review of the floods, which involved record-breaking rainfall, while new flood warnings were issued as further heavy rain threatened the region.

302317_302317.caption: In this Nov 21 2014 file photo President Obama delivers remarks on his executive action on immigration at Del Sol High School in Las Vegas
302317_302317.article_context: A federal judge in Texas issued a preliminary injunction blocking President Obama's immigration policy, which would have deferred deportation for up to 5 million undocumented immigrants. The judge ruled that the administration did not follow proper procedures, particularly public comment requirements, before implementing the policy. The ruling temporarily halts the Deferred Action for Parents of Americans and Lawful Permanent Residents (DAPA) program as a lawsuit from Texas and 26 other states proceeds. The Obama administration said it would appeal the decision, while Texas officials praised the ruling as upholding constitutional checks and balances.

269672_269672.caption: A satellite image taken Thursday morning shows a distinct eye of Hurricane Alex in the Atlantic Ocean
269672_269672.article_context: Hurricane Alex became the first Atlantic hurricane to form in January since 1938, marking only the third January hurricane on record. The National Hurricane Center issued warnings as Alex approached the Azores with 85 mph winds, threatening the islands with heavy rainfall, flash floods, and coastal flooding. Meteorologists attributed Alex’s unusual early formation to record warm ocean waters, influenced in part by global warming, and noted that the Atlantic hurricane season typically runs from June to November. Alex’s arrival begins the new year’s list of storm names, with Bonnie, Colin, and Danielle to follow.

416438_416438.caption: Ronda Rousey celebrates her UFC Bantamweight Title win over Liz Carmouche at the Honda Center in Anaheim California
416438_416438.article_context: Ronda Rousey defeated Liz Carmouche via first-round armbar in the UFC's inaugural women's fight, retaining her bantamweight title and marking her seventh consecutive first-round submission victory. Despite Carmouche briefly threatening Rousey with a neck crank, Rousey regained control and forced a tap-out just before the round ended. Rousey's success led UFC president Dana White to establish a women's division, reversing his earlier position against women's MMA. The historic bout garnered significant media attention, helping pave the way for UFC's commitment to women's fighting and an expanded roster of female athletes.

132434_132434.caption: The Secret Service agents left the stage quickly and Trump finished his speech
132434_132434.article_context: Violence and heightened tensions have marked Donald Trump’s presidential campaign rallies, with incidents including a protester charging the stage and clashes between supporters and opponents leading to arrests and injuries. Trump canceled a Chicago rally due to large-scale protests, raising concerns about the increasingly toxic political atmosphere. His rhetoric, criticized for encouraging division and aggression, has drawn condemnation from both Republican rivals and Democratic leaders, including President Obama, Bernie Sanders, and Hillary Clinton. Despite controversies and escalating unrest, Trump remains the clear frontrunner for the Republican nomination, with key primaries ahead that could determine the direction of his campaign and the party.

716400_716400.caption: Kellingley colliery in Yorkshire the last remaining deep coal mine in the country closes before Christmas
716400_716400.article_context: The history of coal mining in Britain spans from its early use in the 13th century to its industrial expansion, safety innovations, and pivotal labor strikes. Key events include the invention of the miners’ safety lamp in 1815, the nationalisation of the coal industry in 1947, and the miners’ strike of 1984. The industry was privatised in 1994, and by 2001, coal imports surpassed domestic production. In 2015, the UK government announced plans to phase out coal-fired power stations by 2025, and Kellingley colliery, the last deep coal mine, closed later that year.

1567946_1567946.caption: The Israeli military said Hadar Goldin was dragged into a Hamas tunnel
1567946_1567946.article_context: Reports emerged that Israeli soldier Hadar Goldin, suspected to have dual UK-Israeli nationality, was captured by Hamas during fighting in Gaza that broke out just hours into a planned ceasefire. The UK's Foreign Office is investigating Goldin's possible British citizenship, but no confirmation has been given. The incident, which resulted in the deaths of two other Israeli soldiers and intense Israeli shelling in Gaza, led to renewed calls from UK officials and international figures for an unconditional ceasefire amidst rising casualties. Israeli and Palestinian representatives traded accusations over responsibility for the collapse of the truce, while concerns grew over further escalation of the conflict.

1055293_1055293.caption: A fjord behind the town of Ilulissat in Greenland Melting land ice accounts for about half the current rate of sea level rise according to the latest research
1055293_1055293.article_context: A new study by scientists Sarah Purkey, Gregory Johnson, and Don Chambers builds on earlier research to clarify the causes of global sea-level rise. Using advanced measurement techniques, the team confirmed that rising ocean levels are mainly due to both the addition of water from melting ice and the thermal expansion of warming ocean waters. On average, 1.5–1.8 mm of annual sea-level rise comes from meltwater, with the remainder from expansion. The study also reveals significant regional differences in sea-level change, influenced by factors such as gravity shifts due to melting ice, local variations in heat and salt, and wind patterns. Importantly, every ocean layer, even at great depths, contributes to sea-level rise, with mid-depth layers (300–2,000m) playing a larger role than previously thought. The findings highlight increased consistency among scientific methods and mark progress in understanding climate change impacts on the oceans.

1219272_1219272.caption: Shell is planning a drilling project in the Chukchi and Beaufort seas off the northern coast of Alaska
1219272_1219272.article_context: The Obama administration faces growing criticism from Democrats, environmental groups, and Native Alaskan leaders over plans to approve Shell's offshore drilling in the Arctic's Chukchi and Beaufort seas. Despite reassurances from Interior Secretary Ken Salazar about improved safety regulations, opponents warn that drilling in this remote, icy region poses significant environmental risks, especially in the event of an oil spill. The project could begin as early as July, but calls to halt it have intensified following recent concerns about offshore drilling safety.

156544_156544.caption: People watch a large screen showing Japanese Emperor Akihito s video address in Tokyo on Monday REUTERSKim KyungHoon
156544_156544.article_context: Japan's Emperor Akihito delivered a rare televised address, expressing his desire to abdicate due to deteriorating health and concerns about fulfilling his duties. However, Japan's laws currently lack provisions for imperial abdication, so any transition would require parliamentary action. Akihito's statement was carefully worded in line with constitutional restrictions, but made clear his wish to hand over the throne to his son, Crown Prince Naruhito. The government and public have responded supportively, marking a significant moment for Japan's imperial family.

1469339_1469339.caption: Syriza leader Alexis Tsipras is riding a wave of anger directed at the EU
1469339_1469339.article_context: Greece is facing renewed political instability ahead of a snap election on January 25, with the anti-austerity Syriza party leading in opinion polls and threatening to renegotiate the country's EU-IMF bailout terms. Years of excessive spending, unaddressed tax evasion, and inefficiency led to a severe financial crisis in Greece, resulting in massive bailout loans and stringent austerity measures imposed by European lenders. Although Greece has shown signs of economic recovery, ongoing political uncertainty and Syriza's challenge to austerity policies raise concerns about the country’s future in the eurozone. A Syriza victory could inspire similar movements across Europe and potentially disrupt EU efforts to maintain budget discipline, while fears persist that a Greek default or exit from the euro—though less likely than in 2012—could have serious economic repercussions.

610467_610467.caption: A great white shark near Guadalupe Island Mexico unprovoked shark attacks hit an alltime high in 2015
610467_610467.article_context: In 2015, there were 98 unprovoked shark attacks on people worldwide—a record high attributed to rising human populations and increased time spent in the sea. Six people died in these attacks, with fatalities reported in Hawaii, Réunion, Australia, Egypt, and New Caledonia. The United States saw the most attacks, mainly in Florida, followed by Australia and South Africa. Researchers noted that warmer ocean temperatures are pushing shark incidents further north, and while shark populations are declining due to overfishing, increased recreation in the ocean raises the number of encounters. The situation in Réunion is particularly concerning due to a high number of deaths in recent years.

154987_154987.caption: Saudi soldiers fire artillery toward armed vehicles approaching the border with Yemen in Jizan Saudi Arabia in April 2015 The kingdom has been struggling to stop attacks by Yemeni rebels
154987_154987.article_context: Yemeni Houthi rebels have intensified cross-border attacks against southern Saudi Arabia, particularly in Najran, targeting military and civilian locations with rockets and ground incursions. The conflict escalated after a Saudi-led coalition intervened in Yemen to restore the ousted government, resulting in heavy casualties and widespread displacement. Saudi forces are struggling to contain the threat, which has created security and humanitarian challenges while fostering unexpected solidarity between local Ismaili Shiite communities and Saudi authorities. The fighting also takes place amid broader regional instability and financial strain within Saudi Arabia.

1561011_1561011.caption: AlShabab an offshoot of alQaeda have withdrawn from Mogadishu but still launch attacks there
1561011_1561011.article_context: Al-Shabab militants carried out a deadly attack on the SYL Hotel in central Mogadishu, Somalia, using a car bomb and gunfire, resulting in at least nine deaths. An explosion also struck the nearby Peace Garden, a popular public area. The attack, claimed by al-Shabab, an al-Qaeda affiliate, targeted locations near government institutions and followed a mortar attack on the presidential palace earlier in the week. Security forces ended the siege by killing four attackers.

1639421_1639421.caption: A Houthi fighter in Yemen
1639421_1639421.article_context: The Middle East is experiencing widespread instability, marked by ongoing wars in Syria, Iraq, Libya, and Yemen, as well as rising insurgency in Egypt. Central to much of the turmoil is a growing rivalry between Sunni-majority Saudi Arabia and Shia-majority Iran, which is often characterized as a proxy war for regional dominance. This conflict plays out through support for various factions in countries like Syria, Iraq, Lebanon, and Yemen, leading to shifting alliances and complicated interventions, such as the Saudi-led bombing campaign in Yemen against Houthi rebels and cooperation between the U.S. and Iran against Islamic State in Iraq. The ongoing violence has led to severe humanitarian crises, such as the collapse of Syria's education system, while international attention is divided due to other global concerns.

441184_441184.caption: Members of Black Lives Matter continue their encampment Nov 17 2015 outside the Minneapolis Police Department s 4th Precinct as part of a protest over the shooting of Jamar Clark
441184_441184.article_context: Jamar Clark, a 24-year-old Black man, died after being shot by Minneapolis police during a confrontation that began with officers responding to a domestic assault call. Some community members allege Clark was handcuffed when shot, which police dispute. His death led to protests, including dozens of arrests, and demands for transparency. Investigators have collected partial videos of the incident but are withholding them to protect the investigation’s integrity. Minneapolis’s mayor requested a federal civil-rights probe, while two officers involved are on paid leave. Clark had no weapon at the time, and his death has intensified tensions between local police and minority communities.

572551_572551.caption: Protesters in Canberra 2011 to plans in Australia to introduce a price on greenhouse gas emissions
572551_572551.article_context: The article discusses how opponents of climate change action, often aligned with free market and conservative ideologies, use rhetoric centered on 'freedom' and 'liberty' to argue against regulations aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions. It highlights how such groups, including influential think tanks and societies like the Mont Pelerin Society—whose members include prominent political and industry figures—form echo chambers that reinforce climate denial and resist scientific consensus. The author questions the consistency of their opposition to regulation, drawing parallels to past successful government interventions in issues like tobacco, asbestos, and CFCs, and warns that refusal to act on climate change could ultimately undermine the freedoms these groups claim to defend.

584104_584104.caption: Hugh Jackman in Wolverine a box office success despite a pirated copy being leaked online before its release
584104_584104.article_context: At film preview screenings in Leicester Square, attendees are required to surrender their mobile phones as a precaution against pre-release movie piracy, even though industry representatives admit there have been no known cases of movies being pirated from mobile phone recordings. Most pirated pre-release films, including the high-profile Wolverine leak, originate from insider sources or 'screener' copies rather than from camcorders or phones at previews. Meanwhile, leaving many phones in the custody of cinema staff poses a potential data security risk, yet security procedures appear minimal and lack transparency, with no evidence of tamper-evident storage or special insurance for data breaches. The article suggests the film industry should instead focus anti-piracy efforts at the true sources of leaks and calls for better security and transparency regarding the handling of surrendered personal devices.

338263_338263.caption: Crewmembers of Crest Onyx ship prepare to unload parts of AirAsia Flight 8501 in Pangkalan Bun Indonesia on Jan 11
338263_338263.article_context: Divers have recovered both the cockpit voice recorder and flight data recorder from the AirAsia flight that crashed into the Java Sea with 162 people on board. The retrieval of these black boxes is crucial for investigators to determine the cause of the December 28 crash, which preliminary reports suggest may have been linked to poor weather. Authorities continue to analyze the data, and the Indonesian Transport Ministry has claimed AirAsia was not licensed to fly the route on the day of the accident, resulting in a suspension of several airline routes.

389452_389452.caption: Charles Holloway left and Gerardo Martinez leave the courthouse in Banning during the first day of trial May 16 2016
389452_389452.article_context: Surveillance footage of a 2014 arrest in Indio, California, shows former police officer Gerardo Martinez pinning a suspect while officer Charles Holloway punches and kicks him, leading to both officers being fired and the city paying $140,000 to settle an excessive force lawsuit. Though both officers were criminally charged, they were acquitted at trial, and the video provided key evidence. Despite public concern over Holloway's level of force, the Indio Police Department highlighted its swift response, including referring the case for independent investigation. Both officers are now seeking reinstatement to their jobs.

1646056_1646056.caption: Alan Gross back in the US thanked all those who had supported him
1646056_1646056.article_context: Cuban President Raul Castro and US President Barack Obama announced steps to restore diplomatic relations after decades of hostility, including the release of prisoners from both sides. Castro called for the US to end its longstanding trade embargo, which has caused significant damage to Cuba, but lifting the embargo requires approval from the US Congress, where strong opposition remains. The move toward normalization follows over a year of secret negotiations and marks a significant shift in US-Cuba relations since their break in the early 1960s.

1074516_1074516.caption: African Union troops in Somalia
1074516_1074516.article_context: A Human Rights Watch report has accused African Union troops in Somalia of sexually abusing and exploiting vulnerable women and girls, some as young as 12, including cases of rape and trading food aid for sex. The abuses allegedly took place within AU military bases, with soldiers from Burundi and Uganda among those implicated. Despite Amisom’s claim that these are isolated incidents, Human Rights Watch says the cases point to a broader pattern of exploitation and calls for stricter investigation and punishment of offenders. The report highlights the desperation of displaced women amid ongoing conflict and calls for urgent action to prevent further abuse.

243798_243798.caption: Hillary Clinton speaks during a rally at the Charles H Wright Museum of African American History on March 7 2016 in Detroit
243798_243798.article_context: Bernie Sanders won an unexpected victory over Hillary Clinton in the Michigan Democratic primary, bolstering his campaign's momentum and challenging Clinton's strength in industrial states. While Clinton won Mississippi by a wide margin, mainly due to strong support from African-American voters, Sanders' Michigan win undercut arguments that he could not compete in larger, more diverse states. The Michigan result was seen as a response to economic concerns and trade policies, with Sanders appealing to working-class voters affected by job losses. Despite Sanders' win, Clinton retained a significant delegate lead going into upcoming contests, with both candidates emphasizing party unity and positioning themselves for the general election.

382151_382151.caption: Matt Ryan struggled Sunday but the Falcons overcame his three INTs to improve to 30
382151_382151.article_context: The Atlanta Falcons narrowly defeated the Oakland Raiders 23-20, remaining unbeaten and extending their best start in franchise history despite a sloppy performance and three interceptions by quarterback Matt Ryan. Asante Samuel scored a critical 79-yard interception return for a touchdown late in the game, but the Raiders quickly tied it, only for Matt Bryant to secure victory with a 55-yard field goal in the final second. The game featured strong defensive plays, missed opportunities, and a late-game comeback, with Atlanta ultimately prevailing to maintain their perfect record.

67710_67710.caption: President Barack Obama and former President Bill Clinton wave to the crowd after speaking at a campaign event at the New Amsterdam Theatre Monday June 4 2012 in New York
67710_67710.article_context: Former President Bill Clinton is set to officially nominate President Barack Obama at the upcoming Democratic National Convention, where he will make the key economic case for Obama’s reelection. Clinton’s role highlights his continued influence in the party and his effectiveness as a speaker. Although Clinton has occasionally disagreed with Obama’s strategies during the 2012 campaign, his support at the convention is seen as a political asset. The speech positions Clinton at the center of the party’s message, potentially overshadowing Vice President Biden, and has sparked speculation about Hillary Clinton’s future political ambitions.

75530_75530.caption: Peshmerga forces fire a mortar toward Islamic State militants positions
75530_75530.article_context: Iraqi and Kurdish forces, supported by U.S. air power, have launched a major offensive to retake Mosul from ISIS, encountering fierce resistance including explosives, booby traps, and suicide attacks set by the militants. The operation is the largest and most complex against ISIS to date, with forces advancing slowly due to heavy defenses and obstacles. Initial objectives have been achieved, but commanders caution that a difficult battle lies ahead as ISIS fighters dig in and prepare to defend key towns near Mosul. Despite early delays and casualties, officials remain optimistic about the overall success of the campaign.

651561_651561.caption: People queue while they wait to cross the border to Colombia at San Antonio in Tachira state Venezuela on Sunday
651561_651561.article_context: Venezuelan security forces have deported hundreds of Colombians as part of a heightened crackdown on illegal immigrants and contraband along the Colombia-Venezuela border, following an attack on army officers. President Maduro closed a major border crossing, declared a state of emergency, and deployed extra troops to target smuggling and criminal gangs, leading to the deportation of nearly 800 Colombians and disruption for communities on both sides. The actions have increased diplomatic tensions, prompted humanitarian concerns, and drawn criticism from opposition leaders and Colombian officials. Foreign ministers from both nations are set to meet in hopes of resolving the crisis.

826223_826223.caption: Hong Kong chief executive CY Leung said on Monday he was very concerned over the disappearance of five of the city s booksellers
826223_826223.article_context: Agnes Chow, a young pro-democracy activist in Hong Kong, released a viral video criticizing Beijing for the disappearances of five booksellers accused of selling politically sensitive material about Chinese officials. The video highlighted concerns about increasing political suppression and erosion of Hong Kong's freedoms under the 'one country, two systems' agreement. Chow’s message has drawn global attention, while local leaders, including Hong Kong’s chief executive CY Leung, expressed alarm and demanded answers from Beijing regarding the apparent cross-border abductions.

567245_567245.caption: Security checks at JFK airport New York A proposed new scanner will snoop on travellers from 50m away
567245_567245.article_context: The article discusses how heightened security measures and pervasive state surveillance, prompted by the fear of terrorism since 9/11, have dramatically eroded privacy and civil liberties in democratic societies. New technologies such as advanced, discreet molecular scanners are being deployed in airports and borders, enabling authorities to gather extensive personal information without individuals’ awareness or consent. The author argues that these developments reflect a lasting legacy of Osama bin Laden’s impact on Western democracies, as governments justify increasing intrusiveness in the name of security, fundamentally shifting the balance between individual rights and state power.

307055_307055.caption: Cassini makes more news Two craters on Titan show the moon s craters are being readily eroded
307055_307055.article_context: NASA has awarded a $17.8 million contract to Bigelow Aerospace, owned by Robert Bigelow, to install an inflatable space habitat on the International Space Station in 2015, advancing the future of space tourism. Meanwhile, new research using Cassini spacecraft data has revealed that Saturn’s moon Dione likely had a hidden subsurface ocean billions of years ago, which may have caused its massive ridges and cliffs. Scientists believe heat from this ocean helped shape the moon's surface features, providing fresh insights into Saturn's satellites and the potential for future human exploration.

143248_143248.caption: If another round of budget cuts hits the Pentagon Virginia could suffer worse than any other state
143248_143248.article_context: With another round of deep Defense Department spending cuts (sequestration) looming, leaders and analysts in the Washington D.C. region are voicing concerns over the area's heavy reliance on Pentagon funding, particularly in Virginia, which leads the nation in defense-related economic output. Previous sequestration in 2013 caused significant economic stagnation, office vacancies, and consolidation among defense contractors. As Congress has yet to act on budget legislation to avoid further cuts set for October 1, Virginia's senators and governor are urging action and calling for the state to diversify toward private sector growth. Experts warn that continued reductions could harm both immediate regional employment and long-term innovation, as military spending has historically driven development in advanced industries and technology in the region.

1493927_1493927.caption: European law should be applied to a US company the ruling says
1493927_1493927.article_context: The European Court of Justice ruled in favor of Spanish citizen Mario Costeja Gonzalez, requiring Google to remove search results linking to outdated and damaging information about his past financial difficulties. This landmark decision establishes the 'right to be forgotten,' allowing individuals in the EU to request that search engines delist certain personal information from results if it outweighs the public's interest in accessing it. The ruling has significant implications for privacy rights, data protection laws, and global internet companies, with concerns raised about potential censorship and challenges for firms like Google in managing a large volume of removal requests. This decision also affirms the EU's authority to enforce its data privacy rules on non-European companies that serve European users.

1674991_1674991.caption: Protests were held in Sanaa in March calling for the release of Isabelle Prime and her translator Sherine Makkaoui
1674991_1674991.article_context: French citizen Isabelle Prime, who was kidnapped in Yemen in February while working on a World Bank project, has been freed and returned to France. The French government credited Oman for its key role in negotiating her release, and stated that no ransom was paid. Prime’s translator was released earlier, and the kidnappers’ identities remain unknown. The situation highlights ongoing instability in Yemen, where foreigners are frequently abducted amid ongoing conflict and humanitarian crisis.

494817_494817.caption: George Osborne flirted last year with a postelection move to the Foreign Office but has changed his stance as the economy continues to recover
494817_494817.article_context: If the Conservatives win the general election, George Osborne is expected to remain as Britain's chancellor, positioning the Treasury at the center of negotiations over Britain's EU membership. Osborne, who previously considered moving to the Foreign Office, now believes the Treasury should lead the EU talks given its central role in the Scottish referendum and ongoing economic recovery. This move signals Prime Minister David Cameron’s intent to keep Britain in the EU, provided negotiations are successful. The shift in Osborne’s role is likely to deepen tensions with Foreign Secretary Philip Hammond and raise concerns among eurosceptics within the party.

184446_184446.caption: President Obama arrives to address troops at Bagram air base
184446_184446.article_context: The White House accidentally revealed the identity of the CIA’s top officer in Kabul by including his name in a press list distributed to reporters during President Obama’s visit with U.S. troops. The mistake was quickly recognized, and a revised list was issued without the CIA officer’s name, which The Washington Post withheld at the request of the administration, citing security risks. This rare exposure of a CIA operative’s identity prompted concerns about the officer’s safety and the potential need for reassignment, recalling similar incidents such as the Valerie Plame case and exposures of station chiefs in Pakistan.

369618_369618.caption: Israeli F16 aircraft struck a suspected Hezbollah missile shipment in Syria
369618_369618.article_context: Israeli warplanes conducted airstrikes in Syria, targeting missiles believed to be destined for the militant group Hezbollah. The attack, carried out near the port city of Latakia, reportedly struck Russian-made SA-125 missiles, continuing a pattern of Israeli strikes against weapons transfers to Hezbollah. The incident comes as international inspectors announced the completion of dismantling Syria's chemical weapons production facilities.

1148805_1148805.caption: De Boer walks past members of the environmentalist group TckTckTck in Copenhagen
1148805_1148805.article_context: Yvo de Boer, serving as a key figure in UN climate negotiations, played a prominent and emotional role in efforts to develop a successor to the Kyoto Protocol. Despite his optimism about reaching a global climate deal at the Copenhagen summit in 2009, the final agreement was widely criticized as a failure. De Boer became known for his passionate and sometimes tearful advocacy, which helped drive crucial compromises, yet ultimately highlighted the challenges of achieving international consensus on climate action.

1492890_1492890.caption: The Zaatari site in Jordan is currently home to about 80000 refugees
1492890_1492890.article_context: The UK's Department for International Development (DfID) has spent over £1 billion on aid for Syria, distributing funds to both charities and large UN agencies such as UNICEF, the World Food Programme, and UNHCR. Although DfID publishes general breakdowns of where donations go, detailed transparency around how much money actually reaches Syrian refugees through specific projects is lacking, particularly with UN agencies. Significant portions of aid budgets can be consumed by overhead and administrative costs, with estimates suggesting up to half the total may be spent on bureaucracy and management rather than direct assistance. Despite claims from DfID and the UN about efficiency and oversight, the true proportion of aid that benefits Syrians remains unclear due to limited public budget information from multilateral organizations.

1593489_1593489.caption: Dozens of missiles hit Camp Liberty the Iranian group claims
1593489_1593489.article_context: A rocket attack on Camp Liberty in Baghdad killed three members of the Iranian opposition group Mujahideen-e-Khalq (MEK) and injured several others. The MEK and its parent organization, the National Council of Resistance of Iran, attributed the attack to dozens of missiles fired on Thursday evening. Although an Iranian-backed Shia militia claimed responsibility, Iraqi authorities have not officially commented. The US condemned the attack and called on Iraq to improve camp security. The incident reflects ongoing tensions, as Iraq has been working to dismantle MEK camps, and Iran continues to classify the MEK as a terrorist group.

303959_303959.caption: An aerial view of the destroyed island of Homonhon in the aftermath of Typhoon Haiyan on Nov 14
303959_303959.article_context: China pledged only $1.6 million in aid to the Philippines after Typhoon Haiyan, an amount smaller than that given by companies like Ikea and far less than the pledges from the US, Australia, UK, and other countries. This modest response has drawn criticism and is seen as indicative of China’s cautious approach to foreign disaster relief, driven by domestic concerns and strained relations with the Philippines over territorial disputes in the South China Sea. Experts note that while China is a rising economic power and offers some foreign assistance, it is generally reserved about direct humanitarian aid, preferring investments that benefit its own interests.

1081944_1081944.caption: The Sumapaz paramo in Colombia one of numerous paramos declared offlimits to oil gas and mining operations by the country s Constitutional Court
1081944_1081944.article_context: Colombia’s Constitutional Court has struck down a legal loophole that allowed oil, gas, and mining operations in the country’s paramos, unique high-altitude ecosystems vital for water supply to 70% of Colombians. The court declared three paragraphs of a 2015 law unconstitutional, strengthening protections for paramos and affirming that natural resource extraction is banned in these areas. This historic ruling was praised by environmental advocates and is seen as a significant victory for conservation and public access to water. However, the decision leaves the Environment Ministry responsible for delimiting paramo boundaries, raising concerns that some areas might remain vulnerable to resource exploitation depending on government actions.

87808_87808.caption: Mitt Romney pictured criticizes Donald Trump on Thursday
87808_87808.article_context: Mitt Romney, the 2012 Republican presidential nominee, clarified that he is not actively trying to secure the GOP nomination in the current race, but did not completely rule out the possibility of being drafted if a contested convention occurs and no candidate secures a majority of delegates. Romney expressed confidence that one of the four current candidates will ultimately become the nominee, and stated he is not running himself.

1006339_1006339.caption: Smoke billows from a coalfired power station at a steel factory in Hebei China Fixing climate needs far more radical action than proposed currently
1006339_1006339.article_context: With just 12 months left before a critical climate deadline, the article highlights the urgency for meaningful action to avoid uncontrollable climate change. Despite scientific consensus and warnings from bodies like the IPCC, influential industry groups such as the World Coal Association and some governments continue advocating for continued fossil fuel use, slowing progress toward emission cuts. While India defends coal expansion citing 'climate justice' for its development needs, the article contends this approach is ultimately self-destructive. International organizations like UNCTAD propose decentralized, renewable energy solutions as more effective paths to poverty reduction and sustainable prosperity, but such approaches face challenges from entrenched interests. The mounting visibility of climate activism, including symbolic gestures like protesters tattooing atmospheric CO2 levels on themselves, reflects growing societal pressure for system-level change.

1577589_1577589.caption: Labour expects Sadiq Khan to win in London
1577589_1577589.article_context: Labour Party MPs are deeply divided over Jeremy Corbyn’s leadership, with some pushing for his removal amid fears of poor performance in upcoming local and national elections. While Corbyn’s supporters remain confident in his popular backing among party members, opponents are strategizing a possible leadership challenge, debating internal rules that could keep Corbyn off the ballot. Ultimately, membership polls show most Labour members support Corbyn despite potential electoral setbacks, making any attempted coup within the party uncertain and contentious.

1650035_1650035.caption: David Cameron is currently in Brussels meeting other European leaders
1650035_1650035.article_context: The UK has been told by the European Union it must pay an extra £1.7bn towards the EU budget due to its stronger-than-expected economic performance, following a recalculation of member states' contributions. This has sparked strong opposition from British politicians, with some calling for the UK to refuse payment and others demanding a renegotiation of Britain’s relationship with the EU. The demand comes at a politically tense time, ahead of a key by-election and increased support for the anti-EU UK Independence Party. The recalculation affects several countries, with France and Germany set to receive rebates while the UK, Netherlands, and Italy face additional payments. The UK government is considering ways to challenge the EU’s request, which it considers unjust and poorly timed.

61716_61716.caption: View Photo Gallery With the Republican presidential nomination essentially assured former Massachusetts governor Mitt Romney steps up his criticism of President Obama
61716_61716.article_context: Mitt Romney and his wife Ann have each contributed $75,000 to the Romney Victory Fund, the joint fundraising effort supporting his presidential campaign and the Republican National Committee. While Romney is able to give considerably more, this donation is the maximum allowed through this specific channel. The move is seen as an effort to encourage other major donors and demonstrate personal commitment to the campaign. Romney's fundraising efforts have been strong, nearly matching President Obama's totals after clinching the GOP nomination. The campaign has also outlined special perks for top fundraisers but continues to keep most donor identities confidential, in contrast to Obama’s approach.

1123581_1123581.caption: Engraving of the stowage plans of the Liverpool slave ship Brooks
1123581_1123581.article_context: The Smithsonian’s National Museum of African American History and Culture will exhibit artifacts from the wreck of the São José-Paquete de Africa, a Portuguese slave ship that sank near Cape Town in 1794 while transporting over 400 enslaved Africans from Mozambique to Brazil. This marks the first archaeological documentation of a slave ship lost with enslaved people aboard. The recovered objects, including iron ballasts and copper fastenings, will be on long-term loan from the Iziko Museums of South Africa to the Smithsonian, whose new museum is set to open in Washington later this year.

817148_817148.caption: Various unions gather in Norwich for a national oneday strike across the public sector workers gathering at Chapelfield Gardens before walking through the city centre
817148_817148.article_context: On a national one-day strike, thousands of public sector workers—including teachers, council staff, firefighters, and civil servants—walked out across England and Wales to protest against pay, pensions, job cuts, and austerity measures. Major unions such as Unison, NUT, GMB, and TUC led demonstrations in cities including London, Brighton, Liverpool, Newcastle, Bristol, Norwich, and Gateshead. The strike resulted in school closures and large rallies, and was hailed as the largest public sector pay protest against the government since 2010.

227863_227863.caption: Volunteers at St Ignatius food pantry restock items as Larry Bossom left 41 who lost his job a few month ago visits the facility Friday in Chicago
227863_227863.article_context: In the wake of federal food stamp (SNAP) cuts affecting 47 million Americans, food banks nationwide are preparing for a surge in demand as families see reductions in their monthly benefits. The cuts come as Congress fails to provide new funding, forcing many low-income individuals—including seniors, children, and veterans—to rely more heavily on already overstretched food banks. Food bank leaders warn that supplies may not meet increased needs, potentially resulting in shorter lines or smaller food baskets. Further proposed cuts to SNAP in Congress could deepen the crisis for vulnerable communities.

593428_593428.caption: French gendarmes near the scene of the hostagetaking in DammartinenGoele
593428_593428.article_context: Lilian Lepère, a graphic designer who hid for eight hours under a sink during the Charlie Hebdo attacks, is suing French media outlets for broadcasting his presence and endangering his life while the gunmen were in the building. Similar complaints have been raised by survivors of the kosher supermarket attack, where a news channel revealed people were hiding in a fridge during the siege. In response, France’s broadcast regulator censured several networks for serious breaches in their coverage, including revealing sensitive information that put hostages at risk and airing graphic footage of the attacks.

1213120_1213120.caption: A supporter of Mir Hossein Mousavi rests by photos of the former prime minister and former president Mohammad Khatami during a preelection rally in Karaj
1213120_1213120.article_context: Years after Iran's disputed 2009 election and the subsequent Green Movement protests, former demonstrators recall the violence and repression they faced, while physical traces of the movement have largely disappeared. The election of President Hassan Rouhani brought some reform-minded voters back into the political process, but many feel his government has not delivered expected social or political change. While some activists hope for reform through upcoming parliamentary elections, others are skeptical due to ongoing government repression and dominance by conservative factions. International factors, such as regional conflicts and sanctions, further constrain the prospects for pro-democracy activism. Despite setbacks and official crackdowns—like the ban on media coverage of former President Khatami—signs of grassroots support remain, but the movement's future influence is uncertain.

149809_149809.caption: After Wisconsin win Cruz looks for GOP s trust
149809_149809.article_context: After a significant win in the Wisconsin primary, Ted Cruz is making efforts to position himself as a unifying figure for the Republican Party, despite longstanding hostility from GOP establishment members. As Donald Trump continues to lead the race and John Kasich remains a distant contender, the anti-Trump faction within the party is increasingly supporting Cruz as their best chance to block Trump's nomination. Cruz’s new outreach to Republican elites signals his strategy to prevent Trump from reaching the required delegate count and potentially secure the nomination at the convention.

615029_615029.caption: Lightningsparked wildfires along Canada s Hudson Bay are threatening polar bears summer habitat
615029_615029.article_context: The latest UN Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change report highlights significant impacts of climate change on Earth’s ecosystems, with many plant and animal species shifting their ranges toward poles and higher altitudes, and altering seasonal behaviors in response to rising temperatures. Some species, especially those confined to isolated habitats, face increased risk of extinction as they cannot move quickly enough or adapt. Forests are experiencing higher death rates due to drought and pest outbreaks linked to warming, while invasive species are expanding their range. Climate change is causing irreversible changes in Arctic and coral reef ecosystems, affecting key species and leading to food shortages. Whole biomes, such as the tundra and boreal forest, are shifting, threatening habitat for many endemic species.

631251_631251.caption: Amanda Knox after a TV interview in the US after her conviction was upheld
631251_631251.article_context: Raffaele Sollecito, Amanda Knox's former boyfriend, was detained by Italian police after being found near the Austrian border, following an appeal court ruling in Florence that upheld a 25-year prison sentence for his and Knox’s conviction in the 2007 murder of British student Meredith Kercher. Sollecito left the courtroom before the verdict and was later cautioned not to leave Italy, with his passport confiscated. The case marks another development in a long legal process, with previous convictions overturned and retried, and heightened concerns that Sollecito might attempt to flee the country.

1528050_1528050.caption: Liam Neeson plays former CIA agent Bryan Mills who is framed for the murder of his exwife in Taken 3
1528050_1528050.article_context: The thriller sequel Taken 3, starring Liam Neeson, topped the North American box office with $40.4 million, pushing The Hobbit: The Battle of the Five Armies to fourth place after three weeks at number one. Selma and Into the Woods came in second and third, respectively. The strong performance of Taken 3 highlights Neeson's unexpected and continued success as an action star.

1617121_1617121.caption: Argentine Finance Minister Alfonso PratGay said he would eliminate the foreign exchange restrictions that have propped up the peso since 2011
1617121_1617121.article_context: Argentina will end its currency controls, allowing the peso to float freely for the first time in four years. The move, led by newly inaugurated President Mauricio Macri, is expected to result in a sharp devaluation of the peso—in line with the black market rate—and aims to boost exports and spur economic growth. However, consumers and businesses fear this could worsen inflation, which is already high, and reduce purchasing power. The previous government's controls had drained central bank reserves and fueled a thriving black market for US dollars, prompting calls for reform. While businesses gain greater dollar access under the new policy, ordinary Argentines will still face some restrictions.

1616917_1616917.caption: Donald Trump announced the deal during a visit to Prestwick
1616917_1616917.article_context: US billionaire Donald Trump has signed an agreement to use Prestwick Airport as the Scottish base for his private jet and helicopter, following his recent purchase of the nearby Turnberry golf resort. Trump expects the airport to see an increase in international traffic once Turnberry’s £250m renovation is completed. The deal does not include any financial investment by Trump in the airport itself, which was acquired by the Scottish government last year to prevent its closure.

368297_368297.caption: Donald Trump looks on during a rally in WilkesBarre Pa on Oct 10 2016
368297_368297.article_context: Donald Trump escalated his attacks on Republican Party leaders, especially House Speaker Paul Ryan and Senator John McCain, after Ryan announced he would no longer defend or campaign with Trump following the release of a tape in which Trump made vulgar comments about women. This deepened the already significant rift within the GOP, jeopardizing their prospects in the upcoming election and sparking warnings about long-term damage to the party. Trump responded by criticizing both the Republican establishment and his Democratic rival Hillary Clinton, while many Republicans distanced themselves from his candidacy. Political analysts suggested that Trump may be consolidating his base for a post-election movement that could further divide the party.

777260_777260.caption: A Ukrainian soldier carries an unexploded shell during demining works in a field near the eastern city of Mariupol on 23 October 2014
777260_777260.article_context: As Ukraine approaches its parliamentary elections on October 26, the optimistic atmosphere in Kiev contrasts with widespread public anxiety fueled by war in Donbass and deteriorating economic conditions. President Petro Poroshenko’s bloc is favored to win, but its alliance with various power brokers, civil activists, and combatants may lead to a fragmented and conflict-ridden parliament. Radical parties and individuals with limited political experience, including soldiers and activists, are likely to gain significant influence, reflecting a more aggressive and polarized society. Despite hopes for reform and a European future, there is skepticism about the effectiveness of new political entrants and concerns about declining social norms and rule of law. The article concludes that, while the West seeks to support democratic progress, practical and immediate assistance for Ukrainians, along with rigorous election monitoring, should be prioritized.

1591849_1591849.caption: WWII veteran John Saint 82 from London pays his respects at Oosterbeek cemetery as part of the Arnhem anniversary
1591849_1591849.article_context: European and US paratroopers completed commemorative jumps in the Netherlands to mark the 70th anniversary of the Battle of Arnhem, a significant event during World War II's Operation Market Garden where Allied forces suffered heavy losses. The ceremony, involving multinational participation including Germany, honored the thousands who died in the battle, which aimed to end the war but ultimately failed due to strong resistance. The commemoration included remembrance services and reflected on the hopes and tragic realities faced by soldiers and local civilians during the battle.

1084623_1084623.caption: A first world warera poster from the US food administration
1084623_1084623.article_context: The article highlights widespread food waste across various stages of the supply chain, including supermarkets, farms, and food processing facilities. It documents instances such as large amounts of unsold soup, bread, fruit, and vegetables being discarded due to strict retail standards or minor imperfections, and describes practices like the removal and disposal of bread slices for cosmetic reasons. The report underscores the significant quantity of edible food thrown away, drawing attention to the inefficiencies and excesses in modern food distribution and retail systems.

878981_878981.caption: Cumbre Vieja La Palma Canary Islands a collapse of the unstable west flank could spawn a North Atlantic megatsunami
878981_878981.article_context: The 2010 eruption of Iceland’s Eyjafjallajökull volcano caused massive disruption to European air travel, grounding over 107,000 flights and prompting revisions to volcanic risk planning. The article highlights the underappreciated global threat of major volcanic eruptions by recalling the catastrophic 1815 Tambora eruption in Indonesia, which killed tens of thousands locally and led to global climate disruption, famine, and disease in the northern hemisphere. The 'year without a summer' in 1816 brought harsh weather, crop failures, and widespread hunger across Europe and North America. Experts warn that modern societies remain vulnerable to similar or larger eruptions, which could cause global food crises and supply chain disruptions. The article urges improved monitoring and contingency planning, particularly for long-dormant but now-restless volcanoes, listing 10 such sites around the world that currently merit close observation.

1651208_1651208.caption: People in Stein still need convincing about Germany s ability to cope with the influx of refugees
1651208_1651208.article_context: In the village of Stein, Germany, local residents express concerns about the rapid influx of refugees and how the country is changing, reflecting broader national unease. Amid mounting criticism within her Christian Democratic party and declining approval ratings, Chancellor Angela Merkel steadfastly defends her open-door refugee policy at the CDU party conference, rejecting proposals for a cap on refugee numbers and insisting that solutions must be found at the European and international levels. Her speech receives overwhelming support from her party, signaling her continued political strength despite public debate and upcoming regional elections fueled by anti-refugee sentiment. Merkel’s determined stance marks a shift in her leadership style, emphasizing her long-term approach and personal moral conviction.

39531_39531.caption: Iraqi forces fire a M109 selfpropelled howitzer toward the village of Muftuya
39531_39531.article_context: Iraqi and Kurdish forces, supported by U.S. air power, have launched a major offensive to retake Mosul from ISIS, encountering heavy resistance including explosives, booby traps, and fortified defenses. Despite initial successes and collaboration between Iraqi and Kurdish military units, progress has been slow and challenging, with commanders warning of tougher battles ahead in key towns near Mosul. ISIS militants have used suicide attacks and defensive measures to impede the advance, resulting in casualties among coalition forces and highlighting the difficult fight expected as troops move closer to the city.

1562894_1562894.caption: The bullet train line is expected to link Mumbai and Ahmedabad
1562894_1562894.article_context: India's government has approved a $14.7 billion deal with Japan to build the country's first high-speed bullet train line, connecting Mumbai and Ahmedabad and reducing travel time from eight hours to two. The project is considered a major foreign investment in India's outdated railway infrastructure, with Japan providing over half the funding at very low interest rates for 50 years.
