711620_711620.article_context: Twenty Bahraini medics, including Dr. Ali al-Akri, were sentenced to between five and 15 years in prison by a military court on charges including alleged subversive activities and terrorism. Their convictions have drawn widespread international condemnation, highlighting ongoing political repression following the failed uprising in Bahrain. The doctors maintain that their prosecution is politically motivated, stemming from their treatment of injured protesters rather than any real connection to terrorism or foreign agendas. Despite government promises of reform, opposition leaders and medics report worsening conditions and continued crackdowns, while the regime, supported by Saudi Arabia, justifies its actions as necessary to maintain stability.

425530_425530.caption: Boston Marathon bombing survivor Marc Fucarile seated talks to his son Gavin 6 as Carlos Arredondo stands behind them at the finish line of the Boston Marathon
425530_425530.article_context: One year after the devastating Boston Marathon bombings that killed three and injured over 260, survivors, first responders, and a resilient city gather for remembrance and celebration. The marathon continues with heightened security and record participation, symbolizing Boston's strength and recovery. Key figures like survivor Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs and has since rebuilt his life, and Carlos Arredondo, the heroic 'man in the cowboy hat,' return to honor those affected, reflecting on healing, gratitude, and the lasting impact of their actions. The event highlights both personal recovery and collective unity in the face of tragedy.

96764_96764.caption: President Obama speaks about Iraq in the Brady Briefing room of the White House on June 19
96764_96764.article_context: The Obama administration is now treating the instability in Syria and Iraq as a connected crisis, with the rise of the al-Qaeda-inspired ISIS posing a threat to both governments and regional stability. President Obama and his advisers are debating military and political options, including possible airstrikes in Iraq and expanded support for moderate Syrian rebels, while grappling with challenges posed by sectarian divisions and porous borders. The administration recognizes that effective counterterrorism strategies must address both countries together, though responses will differ. U.S. support for Iraqi Prime Minister Maliki remains uneasy amid criticisms and concerns about his ability to address the crisis, while Obama continues to oppose Syria's Assad. The situation has been complicated by previous decisions, changing regional dynamics, and the rapid advance of Islamist insurgents.

176155_176155.caption: Bernie Sanders works the crowd after a Get Out the Vote Rally at Great Bay Community College s gymnasium in Portsmouth
176155_176155.article_context: Senator Marco Rubio's momentum in the Republican presidential race was disrupted following a debate in which he repeatedly used a scripted talking point, drawing criticism and mockery from rivals and the media. The incident cast doubt on Rubio's authenticity and experience, reviving the campaigns of Chris Christie, Jeb Bush, and John Kasich ahead of the New Hampshire primary. Donald Trump maintained his lead, but Rubio's stumble contributed to a more volatile and competitive race, with several candidates now vying for second place and the mainstream Republican vote remaining divided.

124734_124734.caption: DC considers most generous family medical leave plan in US
124734_124734.article_context: The D.C. Council is set to introduce legislation that would give nearly all part-time and full-time workers in Washington, D.C. up to 16 weeks of paid family leave—the most generous such program in the United States. Funded by a new tax on employers, the plan would cover 100% of pay for workers earning up to $52,000 and partial pay above that, and is designed to support new parents, caregivers, and those recovering from illness. Backed by the Obama administration as a model for national reform, the bill faces resistance from the business community, which warns it could harm competitiveness, but is seen by supporters as a significant step toward addressing wage inequality and expanding worker benefits.

751212_751212.caption: Kevin Rudd tours an apprenticeship organisation in Gladstone Queensland a month before the campaign and a day after his toolbox announcement
751212_751212.article_context: During Kevin Rudd's brief return as Prime Minister ahead of the 2013 election, his campaign team scrambled to develop last-minute policies in response to poor polling, including a $34 million apprentice payment plan and a controversial Northern Territory company tax cut that surprised his own frontbenchers. Rudd also announced the 'PNG solution' to send asylum seekers to Papua New Guinea or Manus Island. Labor strategist Bruce Hawker, in his campaign diary, reveals the chaotic, reactive nature of policy-making during the campaign, arguing Rudd saved Labor from electoral disaster despite internal tension and a lack of preparedness. The diary also details the failed strategy around party costings and Rudd’s brief contemplation of remaining leader on election night before deciding to step down.

1480598_1480598.caption: Kirsty Williams is named in Tim Farron s team to lead the Lib Dem fightback after election defeat
1480598_1480598.article_context: New Liberal Democrat leader Tim Farron has announced his party's cabinet, with Welsh Liberal Democrat Mark Williams being the only one of the eight MPs left out, although he will receive a key campaign role in August. Kirsty Williams will serve as spokeswoman for Wales, while Baroness Randerson will handle the transport brief. Farron expressed confidence that his team will lead the party’s revival, and noted that several cabinet members are not MPs or peers.

296469_296469.caption: Pensioners wait for the opening of the National Bank of Greece to withdraw a maximum of 120 euros for the week in central Athens Photo is from July 15 2015
296469_296469.article_context: Greece’s parliament approved tough austerity measures required by international creditors to secure a $100 billion bailout, the country’s third rescue package in five years. The vote passed with a clear majority despite significant defections from Prime Minister Tsipras' own Syriza party and widespread public protests, including clashes with police in Athens. The bailout will result in higher taxes, pension cuts, and sale of state assets, sparking strong opposition among Greeks affected by years of austerity. Following the passage, the European Central Bank increased emergency funding and eurozone finance ministers agreed to move forward with a three-year bailout, although disagreements remain over potential debt relief for Greece.

269610_269610.caption: Hillary Clinton arrives with Sen Tim Kaine DVa at a rally at Florida International University Panther Arena in Miami on July 23 2016
269610_269610.article_context: Hillary Clinton introduced Tim Kaine as her vice presidential running mate, emphasizing his progressive credentials and readiness to assume the presidency. During their debut rally in Miami, Kaine discussed his working-class background and criticized Republican nominee Donald Trump, while Clinton highlighted Kaine's experience and opposition to Trump’s policies. The announcement aimed to appeal to independent and moderate voters, though some progressive Democrats expressed concern over Kaine’s support for issues like the Trans-Pacific Partnership. The selection took place as the Democratic National Convention approached, with party leaders hoping to contrast their message with the negativity of the Republican convention and unite supporters after a contentious primary.

1685012_1685012.caption: Jacques Chirac with his wife Bernadette and Alan Juppe at a memorial ceremony in April 2002
1685012_1685012.article_context: The possibility of Nicolas Sarkozy returning as a candidate for the French presidency in 2017 has caused division, with former President Jacques Chirac supporting Alain Juppe instead. Sarkozy recently began his comeback campaign for leadership of the UMP party, which could lead to a presidential run. Meanwhile, Chirac's wife criticized Juppe's appeal, and Sarkozy faces renewed legal troubles over alleged campaign finance fraud. Polls indicate public opposition to Sarkozy's return, with a majority of voters not supporting his candidacy.

307334_307334.caption: Dec 1 2013 Al Jefferson can only watch as Chris Bosh sinks one of his three crucial 3s in the fourth quarter of the Heat s 10th straight win
307334_307334.article_context: The Los Angeles Lakers and Cleveland Cavaliers are in trade talks involving Pau Gasol and Andrew Bynum, primarily motivated by financial considerations rather than on-court impact. The Lakers are exploring this deal to ease luxury tax burdens, given Bynum's contract can be waived before a deadline for substantial savings. However, as of Saturday night, the Cavs have only offered a second-round pick, which the Lakers consider insufficient, and key details remain unresolved. The outcome hinges on whether the Lakers hold out for a better asset or settle for financial relief before the unofficial Sunday deadline.

669040_669040.caption: A peshmerga fighter plants a Kurdish flag as Iraqi Kurdish forces push into Isis territory 20 miles southwest of Kirkuk
669040_669040.article_context: Kurdish authorities in Iraq have accused Islamic State militants of using chlorine gas as a chemical weapon against peshmerga fighters during a January suicide truck bomb attack near Mosul. The Kurdistan Region Security Council reported that gas canisters containing chlorine were found at the attack site, and dozens of fighters experienced symptoms of chemical exposure. While similar allegations have been made previously about ISIS employing chemical weapons, there has been no independent confirmation, and international organizations have not yet commented. The report comes as Iraqi forces, including militias and tribesmen, continue their offensive to recapture Tikrit from the militants.

309936_309936.caption: Republican presidential candidates John Kasich left and Ted Cruz right say they have joined forces to keep frontrunner Donald Trump from getting the delegates he needs for the GOP nomination
309936_309936.article_context: Republican presidential candidates Ted Cruz and John Kasich formed a strategic alliance aimed at preventing Donald Trump from securing the 1,237 delegates needed to win the GOP nomination. Under the plan, Cruz will focus his campaign on Indiana, while Kasich shifts attention to Oregon and New Mexico, effectively clearing Cruz's path in the crucial May 3 Indiana primary. The alliance comes as Trump maintains his lead with 845 delegates and as opponents seek to force a contested convention if Trump falls short of a delegate majority. Trump criticized the move, claiming the system is 'rigged.' Indiana's delegate allocation and upcoming primaries are viewed as pivotal in determining whether Trump can clinch the nomination outright.

111118_111118.caption: This video image shows El Chapo being escorted into a vehicle in Los Mochis Mexico after his arrest
111118_111118.article_context: Joaquin 'El Chapo' Guzman, leader of the Sinaloa cartel, escaped from Mexico's Altiplano maximum security prison via a sophisticated, nearly mile-long tunnel equipped for easy passage. Guzman's organization is renowned for constructing advanced drug tunnels along the U.S.-Mexico border, using engineering expertise to facilitate smuggling operations and evade law enforcement. These well-designed tunnels, which have been discovered primarily in California and Arizona, have played a major role in the cartel’s criminal success and highlight both the cartel’s ingenuity and the ongoing security challenges faced by authorities.

684555_684555.caption: Metal snares are often impossible for chimps to remove This trip Lanjo tried but failed Eventually staff with the the Kibale Chimpanzee Project removed his snare
684555_684555.article_context: Wire snares set by poachers in Uganda’s Kibale National Park have become a pervasive and devastating threat to wildlife, gravely injuring or killing animals such as chimpanzees, elephants, and leopards. About one third of the park’s chimps suffer from snare wounds, as illustrated by Max, a double-amputee chimpanzee. Since 1997, specialized teams of rangers have worked to remove over 6,500 snares, risking their lives in confrontations with poachers and wild animals. The Kibale Snare Removal Programme, supported by local and international organizations, also prioritizes community outreach and education to address the root causes of snaring, which range from poverty to cultural traditions. Efforts continue to save wildlife and help local populations understand the value of conservation, but snares remain a persistent and underreported crisis impacting both animal welfare and the forest ecosystem.

234865_234865.caption: Secretary of State Hillary Clinton testifies before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee about the attack in Benghazi
234865_234865.article_context: During Congressional hearings on the 2012 Benghazi attack, outgoing Secretary of State Hillary Clinton faced intense questioning from Republican senators about the administration’s handling and messaging of the incident, which resulted in the deaths of four Americans. Clinton vigorously defended her actions and those of the State Department, making a notable statement, 'What difference, at this point, does it make?' regarding the cause of the attack. While supporters praised her service and accomplishments, her remarks and the Benghazi incident remain points of controversy that could impact her political legacy and prospects for a potential 2016 presidential run.

1558315_1558315.caption: The court heard Melnyk and Brown blamed Mr MacKay for their friend s death
1558315_1558315.article_context: Dean Melnyk and Andrew Brown were sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 20 years for the murder of Kevin MacKay, whom they blamed for supplying the ecstasy tablet that killed their teenage friend Jamie Abba. The men carried out a premeditated and brutal stabbing attack on MacKay in Ecclefechan last August, shortly after Abba's funeral. The murder deeply affected the small community, leading to increased police efforts to maintain calm and support those impacted. The judge condemned the vigilante nature of the crime, emphasizing the severity and premeditation involved.

95716_95716.caption: Iraqi Islamic State leader purported to make public appearance
95716_95716.article_context: A rare video was released showing Islamic State leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi giving a speech in a mosque in Mosul, marking an unusual public appearance for the reclusive figure. The video drew attention not only for Baghdadi's message and claim of the new caliphate but also for his apparent wearing of a luxury watch, which some speculated to be expensive. However, the focus on the watch distracts from the key point: Baghdadi is alive and visibly asserting his leadership, despite prior rumors of his death.

1585658_1585658.caption: Tunisia has seen a rise in Islamist militancy since 2011
1585658_1585658.article_context: Islamic State claimed responsibility for a deadly attack on a tourist resort in Sousse, Tunisia, where a gunman killed at least 38 people—mostly foreign visitors. The attacker was identified as Seifeddine Rezgui, a student unknown to authorities. This incident follows a similar attack by IS on the Bardo museum earlier in the year and highlights Tunisia’s ongoing struggle with Islamist militancy since the 2011 uprising. Despite efforts to control the threat, attacks are increasing, targeting both tourists and the state, which poses serious risks to the country's vital tourism industry.

1104173_1104173.caption: Michael Gove told the BBC Demotion emotion promotion locomotion I don t know how you would describe this move
1104173_1104173.article_context: Prime Minister David Cameron conducted a major cabinet reshuffle, notably demoting his close ally Michael Gove from education secretary to chief whip, following concerns that Gove had become unpopular among teachers and entangled in disputes with colleagues. The reshuffle aimed to improve the Conservative Party’s image ahead of the upcoming general election, particularly by increasing the number of women in senior government roles, though the change was limited. Notable appointments included Liz Truss as environment secretary and Nicky Morgan as education secretary, while Philip Hammond was promoted to foreign secretary. The moves demonstrated Cameron's willingness to assert control over his team, but also drew criticism for insufficient progress on gender balance and exposed internal party tensions.

365654_365654.caption: Park entrance sign at Yellowstone National Park A tourist crashed a drone into Grand Prismatic Spring on Saturday Aug 2 2014
365654_365654.article_context: A tourist crashed a drone into Yellowstone National Park's Grand Prismatic Spring, raising concerns about potential damage to the famous hot spring. The incident occurred shortly after drones were banned in all U.S. national parks, and the pilot informed officials before leaving the area. Park rangers are now investigating the crash and considering how to safely locate and remove the drone, fearing it could obstruct the spring's water flow or cause further harm.

1541599_1541599.caption: MS Fram became surrounded by fast moving ice in Antarctic Sound
1541599_1541599.article_context: The Royal Navy vessel HMS Protector rescued the Norwegian cruise ship MS Fram after it became trapped by fast-moving ice in Antarctic Sound. HMS Protector broke through four-metre thick ice over a two-hour operation, freeing the ship without injuries. The rescue highlights the unpredictable conditions of Antarctica and the capabilities of the Royal Navy's ice patrol. HMS Protector continued its patrol and support of inspections in the region following the incident.

180640_180640.caption: A goose chases off a mallard duck that had been harassing other ducks around a cove on North River at Wildwood Park in Bridgewater Va
180640_180640.article_context: Research shows that older female elephants, known as matriarchs, play a vital role in the social structure and survival of elephant herds. Studies at Amboseli National Park in Kenya reveal that matriarchs lead complex family networks and use their experience to guide group decisions, especially in finding food, water, and avoiding dangers like predators. Elephants defer to the knowledge of older matriarchs, who are better at making survival decisions and recognizing threats. Poaching, which targets older elephants for their tusks, disrupts these family structures, leading to increased stress, weaker social bonds, and reduced reproductive success. While elephant groups show resilience, the loss of matriarchs has significant negative impacts, highlighting the importance of protecting these leaders for the well-being of elephant populations.

193154_193154.caption: Brenda Brown right meets with volunteers in front of the DC General shelter where Relisha once lived to hand out toiletries to the homeless after the service at the church
193154_193154.article_context: Andrea Tatum was found murdered in a Maryland motel room during the police search for missing 8-year-old Relisha Rudd. Authorities concluded that Andrea's husband, Kahlil Tatum, killed her with a gunshot before later committing suicide with the same weapon. Kahlil Tatum was a custodian at the shelter where Relisha lived, and her disappearance remains unsolved, as Tatum took key information about her whereabouts to his grave. The case highlights deep mysteries surrounding both Andrea’s death and Relisha's vanishing, raising questions about family dynamics, why Relisha was allowed to spend time with Tatum, and what Andrea may have known prior to her killing.

142937_142937.caption: British Prime Minister David Cameron speaks to supporters at Hayesfield Girls School on May 4 in Bath southwest England while on the UK general election campaign trail
142937_142937.article_context: As Britain heads into a crucial election, Prime Minister David Cameron has shown unusual intensity on the campaign trail, rallying supporters and attacking the opposition Labour Party for past economic mismanagement. Facing a surprisingly close race against Labour leader Ed Miliband, Cameron highlights his government’s economic achievements but struggles with a divided electorate and criticisms of his centrist and sometimes inconsistent leadership. Observers note his promises on issues from same-sex marriage to the EU referendum, while critics point to his political calculations and retreat from global affairs. With polls uncertain, Cameron’s political future—and the direction of the Conservative Party—hangs in the balance.

171088_171088.caption: Trump backs out of final debate before Iowa caucus
171088_171088.article_context: Republican presidential front-runner Donald Trump announced that he will not participate in the upcoming Fox News GOP debate, citing an ongoing feud with the network and objections to moderator Megyn Kelly, whom he has accused of treating him unfairly. Trump’s decision, which his campaign described as final, comes just days before the Iowa caucuses and is seen as a bold move to shape the campaign narrative. Instead of attending the debate, Trump plans to hold a competing event to raise money for veterans. The announcement drew criticism and mockery from his rivals, especially Ted Cruz, and has raised questions about Trump’s willingness to face tough scrutiny. Fox News and the Republican National Committee both stated they would not alter their plans, and Megyn Kelly will remain as a moderator.

922144_922144.caption: Worker red ants tending pupae in nest Powys Wales A study published this week says wildlife decline threatens UK s biodiversity
922144_922144.article_context: The news article showcases a series of wildlife and nature events from around the world, including severe flooding in northern England caused by Storm Desmond, migratory bird activity in Hungary, and environmental challenges such as oil spills affecting birds in Russia and polluted fog in India. It highlights conservation efforts like the birth of Siberian tiger cubs in Russia, threats to iconic species including the Andean condor and Maasai Mara lions, and features a variety of animal sightings across diverse habitats, underscoring both the beauty and vulnerability of global wildlife.

1608789_1608789.caption: Iraq has seen a spate of violence in the past few days with attacks on both Sunni and Shia targets
1608789_1608789.article_context: A car bomb in Baghdad's mainly Shia Jadida district killed at least eight people and injured around 20, following a suicide bombing at a nearby Shia mosque and a series of deadly attacks targeting both Shia and Sunni communities. The recent violence has heightened sectarian tensions in Iraq amid the advance of Islamic State militants. Efforts to form a more inclusive government under Prime Minister-designate Haider al-Abadi have suffered setbacks, as key Sunni politicians suspended talks after a massacre at a Sunni mosque.

1539742_1539742.caption: The Ganges is India s most heavily polluted river
1539742_1539742.article_context: India's National Green Tribunal harshly criticised both federal and Uttar Pradesh governments for their failure to clean up the polluted Ganges river, despite promises and substantial spending. The watchdog was responding to a petition highlighting ongoing practices such as dumping dead bodies in the river, especially in Varanasi. The Ganges, a sacred river for Hindus and a critical resource for millions, continues to suffer from unchecked industrial waste, sewage, and religious practices that contribute to its pollution. Environmental activists and observers note that despite Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s pledge to restore the river and significant funds allocated to the cleanup, meaningful progress has not been achieved.

1601113_1601113.caption: Last year 46 Turkish citizens were held hostage for three months by Islamic State
1601113_1601113.article_context: Eighteen Turkish construction workers were kidnapped by armed men in military uniforms in Baghdad's Sadr City while working on a sports stadium project. The kidnappers, who remain unidentified, took the workers at dawn, and authorities in both Iraq and Turkey have yet to determine who is responsible. The incident occurs amid ongoing abductions in the area, some linked to Shia militias and criminal gangs. Turkish officials are in contact with Iraqi authorities, and the kidnapping highlights the persistent security risks faced by Turkish nationals working in Iraq.

1179582_1179582.caption: Bill Clinton with journalists Laura Ling and Euna Lee after the former US president negotiated their release from North Korea
1179582_1179582.article_context: The US government has announced a new grant program, offering up to $350,000 to support projects that promote human rights and democracy in North Korea, including efforts to physically move information into and out of the country. While some human rights activists see these initiatives as necessary for change, many experts express concern that such activities could seriously endanger North Koreans and foreign participants, as possessing or smuggling foreign media is illegal and harshly punished in North Korea and China. Critics also question the effectiveness and ethical implications of the approach, noting that the program discourages academic or engagement-based projects and may lack a broader strategic vision for improving North Korea’s human rights situation.

1646587_1646587.caption: iPhone users in Germany have no push email service from Apple
1646587_1646587.article_context: Apple has been compelled to halt push email services for iCloud and MobileMe users on iOS devices in Germany following a court ruling that Apple’s technology infringed a Motorola Mobility patent. While users can still receive emails manually, automatic delivery is disabled. Apple is appealing the decision, arguing the patent is invalid. The litigation only affects iOS devices in Germany, not computers or other services. This restriction is part of ongoing patent disputes between Apple and Motorola Mobility, including previous injunctions and rulings over other smartphone features. Google, which is acquiring Motorola Mobility, will take control of its substantial patent portfolio.

1621155_1621155.caption: The Supreme Court ruling has come as a huge shock to many in India
1621155_1621155.article_context: India's Supreme Court has reinstated Section 377, a colonial-era law criminalizing gay sex, overturning the 2009 Delhi High Court decision that had decriminalized homosexual acts. The ruling is seen as a major setback for LGBTQ rights, drawing strong reactions from various segments of society—some supporting the verdict as preservation of traditional values, while activists condemned it for violating constitutional rights and equality. The decision has sparked widespread debate about minority rights, cultural values, and the future of LGBTQ advocacy in India.

1630763_1630763.caption: The bus attack is the latest in a series of strikes by the Taliban in the Afghan capital
1630763_1630763.article_context: A suicide bomber killed at least six Afghan soldiers near Kabul, targeting a military bus in an attack claimed by the Taliban. This marks the group's first attack in the capital in over a week and comes amid increased Taliban violence as foreign combat troops prepare to withdraw from Afghanistan. Despite President Ashraf Ghani's promises of peace, Kabul continues to experience regular militant bombings. After the withdrawal, 12,000 NATO troops will remain for training and support, while a separate US-led force will assist Afghan soldiers in operations against the Taliban.

1585588_1585588.caption: Leonid Papachin performed the manoeuvre in a 40tonne truck on the M6 Toll in Lichfield Staffordshire
1585588_1585588.article_context: Leonid Papachin, a lorry driver, was caught on camera dangerously attempting a U-turn on the M6 Toll motorway after driving the wrong way up an exit slip-road in Staffordshire. He pleaded guilty to dangerous driving and was sentenced to a 15-week suspended prison term, given an 18-month driving ban, and ordered to pay costs. Authorities hope the incident will deter others from endangering motorists by violating motorway regulations.

1635130_1635130.caption: The US says there are thousands possibly tens of thousands of civilians inside Ramadi
1635130_1635130.article_context: Iraqi forces, supported by US-led air strikes and Sunni tribal fighters, have launched a major offensive to retake Ramadi from Islamic State militants. Troops entered several key districts and are advancing towards the city's main government complex, encountering IS resistance mainly through snipers and suicide bombers. The recapture of Ramadi, a significant Sunni stronghold, would mark an important victory for Iraq, boost morale, and showcase the role of Sunni tribesmen in the fight against IS. Concerns remain over civilian safety, with reports of IS using residents as human shields. This operation is part of a wider campaign that has seen IS lose substantial territory in Iraq and Syria over the past year.

109082_109082.caption: Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump speaks during a campaign rally in Redding Calif on June 3 2016
109082_109082.article_context: On the same night Hillary Clinton secured the Democratic nomination, becoming the first woman at the top of a major party ticket, Donald Trump claimed he had 'broken the glass ceiling' for women in the construction industry and defended his record on women's issues. Trump's remarks, made on Fox News, drew criticism and mockery on social media, particularly due to their timing as the nation focused on Clinton's historic achievement. He also criticized Clinton's honesty and leadership abilities, stating she would be a 'disaster' as president.

463787_463787.caption: The first live sighting of a Sumatran rhino in Kalimantan the Indonesia part of Borneo in over 40 years
463787_463787.article_context: Conservationists in Indonesian Borneo have physically encountered a Sumatran rhino for the first time in more than 40 years, capturing a female estimated to be four to five years old. The critically endangered hairy rhino species now numbers fewer than 100 individuals due to hunting and habitat loss, with their last wild populations remaining in Sumatra and Kalimantan. Experts hailed the discovery as extraordinary, as these animals are extremely elusive and have previously only been detected through indirect evidence. The captured rhino will be relocated to a sanctuary to ensure its safety, and hopes persist that such breakthroughs could help the species survive, despite ongoing challenges like limited funding and political support.

163504_163504.caption: Justice Antonin Scalia passed away on Saturday creating an unusual vacancy on the Supreme Court
163504_163504.article_context: The death of Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia in an election year has sparked debate over whether President Obama should nominate a replacement, as conservative lawmakers argue it's not standard to confirm justices during election years. While some, like Sen. Ted Cruz, claim there's long precedent against election-year confirmations, history shows that such vacancies are rare and that past appointments—such as Justice Kennedy in 1988—did occur in election years under specific circumstances. The Constitution and past practice offer ambiguous guidance, leaving the process largely to political interpretation and debate.

252410_252410.caption: Attorney General Eric Holder left and Education Secretary Arne Duncan are warning public schools against restricting or discouraging undocumented immigrants from enrolling in K12 public schools
252410_252410.article_context: The Obama administration announced new guidance requiring public schools to enroll all students regardless of immigration status and prohibiting policies that discourage undocumented immigrants from attending. This move reinforces the federal law and the Plyler v. Doe Supreme Court decision, which bars schools from excluding undocumented children. Attorney General Eric Holder and Education Secretary Arne Duncan emphasized the importance of equal access and warned schools against discriminatory enrollment practices. The announcement follows recent state and local measures that sought to restrict access for undocumented students, with officials clarifying acceptable forms of residency documentation and reiterating that lack of a Social Security number cannot bar enrollment.

70804_70804.caption: Brady takes DeflateGate suspension to court
70804_70804.article_context: NFL and players' union lawyers are set to meet in a U.S. District Court in New York for a settlement conference regarding Tom Brady's four-game suspension for his alleged role in DeflateGate. Judge Richard M. Berman will personally oversee the mediation, seeking a resolution before moving to trial. Though the hearing will begin with public statements, most deliberations will take place privately. No immediate conclusion is expected, as negotiations may extend into the next month, with further briefings and arguments scheduled if no settlement is reached. Both parties have asked the judge to rule before the NFL season begins.

924716_924716.caption: Ed Miliband arrives at Paddington station in London on his way to Cardiff to talk about immigration and hold a people s question time with the public
924716_924716.article_context: As the UK election campaign intensifies, political leaders from major parties travel across the country to engage with voters and present their policies. Ed Miliband, Nick Clegg, George Osborne, Nigel Farage, and Nicola Sturgeon make public appearances, deliver speeches on key issues such as immigration and the economy, and interact with local communities. The campaign atmosphere is highlighted by public events, candidate visits to businesses, and campaign posters—some of which have been defaced—reflecting the lively and contested nature of the election.

153451_153451.caption: No campaigners celebrate as results come in at the Scottish independence referendum count at the Royal Highland Centre in Edinburgh Scotland
153451_153451.article_context: Scottish voters chose to remain part of the United Kingdom in a highly anticipated referendum, with 55 percent voting against independence and 45 percent in favor. The decision ended a fervent campaign marked by record-high voter turnout and deep divisions among Scots. Independence leader Alex Salmond conceded defeat and emphasized accepting the democratic result, while unionist leaders celebrated the outcome as preserving the 307-year-old union. In response, British leaders face pressure to deliver on promises for greater Scottish autonomy made during the campaign. The vote was closely watched internationally and is expected to shape relations within the UK for years to come.

743718_743718.caption: Wisconsin police found the unnamed victims Sunday morning in a residence in Piehl One had been shot and the other stabbed according to the sheriff s office
743718_743718.article_context: Ashlee Martinson, a 17-year-old girl described as 'armed and dangerous,' was arrested in Indiana after a nationwide alert following the double murder of her relatives in northern Wisconsin. Martinson and her boyfriend, Ryan Sisco, were found driving hundreds of miles from the crime scene, though Sisco is not a suspect but wanted for questioning. The victims, discovered in a remote Wisconsin residence, died from shooting and stabbing. Martinson is being charged as an adult in Wisconsin and awaits extradition to face charges.

154804_154804.caption: Rep Steve King on GOP s immigration platform Walls do nt have prosecutorial discretion
154804_154804.article_context: The Washington Post hosted a series of live events during the Republican National Convention in Cleveland, featuring political briefings, discussions on major issues such as trade, energy, immigration, national security, and health care, and interviews with key figures including politicians and experts. The events included panels with policymakers, opinion writers, and special guests, offering behind-the-scenes insights into the GOP platform and the 2016 presidential campaign. The Post also organized interactive activities like trivia nights and viewing parties, providing comprehensive coverage and engagement for attendees throughout the convention.

528289_528289.caption: Shinzo Abe centre is led by a Shinto priest as he visits Yasukuni shrine in 2013 Abe did not visit in person this year but instead sent a ritual offering
528289_528289.article_context: Japan’s prime minister, Shinzo Abe, has signaled he will not repeat explicit apologies for Japan’s wartime actions in his upcoming statement marking the anniversary of the end of the Pacific war, a shift from previous leaders’ stances. Abe’s cautious approach is expected to provoke anger among China and South Korea, who demand recognition and apology for Japan’s past colonial aggression and wartime atrocities, including the issue of 'comfort women.' Ahead of key diplomatic visits, including meetings with Chinese and US leaders, Abe made a ritual offering rather than personally visiting the controversial Yasukuni shrine to avoid further international criticism. These moves highlight simmering tensions over historical memory in East Asia and Abe’s intent to soften Japan's acknowledgment of its wartime past.

343794_343794.caption: Palestinian medics carry a body from Gaza s eastern Shejaiya district on July 20 2014
343794_343794.article_context: On the bloodiest day of the ongoing Gaza conflict, at least 65 Palestinians and 13 Israeli soldiers were killed in heavy fighting in a Gaza City neighborhood, prompting international concern and calls for civilian protection. The UN held an emergency session as criticism mounted over the civilian toll, while Hamas claimed to have captured an Israeli soldier—a claim denied by Israel. The battle involved intense tank fire, destruction of homes, and forced mass evacuations, with hundreds wounded and thousands displaced. President Obama urged for a cease-fire and Secretary of State John Kerry was sent to aid negotiations, but Hamas rejected a previous Egyptian-brokered truce, demanding an end to the blockade and border closures. As casualties rose and conditions worsened, residents expressed a desire for peace but insisted any cease-fire must address the underlying issues of siege and deprivation.

1580258_1580258.caption: Texts from the Tera system were originally used to help combat cholera in Haiti
1580258_1580258.article_context: The Red Cross and Red Crescent plan to expand their SMS-based emergency alert system, originally used for Ebola response in Sierra Leone, to seven additional West African countries. The system, called Trilogy Emergency Relief Application (Tera), enables rapid delivery of health and crisis information and tailored replies via text to people in affected areas, without compromising user privacy. Its effectiveness in Sierra Leone, particularly for public health campaigns, has led to this initiative, which depends on cooperation from local authorities and mobile networks. The system is designed to minimize spam complaints and network overload, and can be used for epidemics, disaster warnings, and relief coordination.

1042130_1042130.caption: Melita Bela Celis lives in San Pedro village a Kukama Indian community on the shore of Maranon river where fish have been devastated by the oil spill
1042130_1042130.article_context: While environmental leaders assembled in Lima to discuss climate change solutions, a series of five major oil spills from the state-owned Petroperú pipeline devastated the Peruvian Amazon, contaminating rivers and fishing lagoons relied on by indigenous communities. The spills have caused widespread illness, mass fish deaths, and irreparable damage to local livelihoods, highlighting the contradiction between Peru's stated commitments to renewable energy and its aggressive expansion of oil operations. Indigenous leaders and environmental campaigners blame decades of pipeline neglect and weakened environmental regulations for the disaster, accusing the government of prioritizing oil industry interests over environmental and community health.

71631_71631.caption: Afghans protest in Kabul in November after seven people from the Hazara minority group were beheaded by Taliban militants
71631_71631.article_context: The beheading of a 9-year-old Hazara girl by Taliban insurgents in Afghanistan galvanized the Hazara community and sparked massive protests in Kabul, demanding better protection for the Shiite minority. The attack highlighted a rise in violence and abductions against Hazaras since the withdrawal of NATO troops, with multiple groups targeting them for their ethnicity. Despite promises from President Ghani to improve security and promote ethnic harmony, Hazaras continue to face discrimination, insecurity, and limited opportunities. The killing has become a rallying point for broader Hazara grievances about marginalization and threats from various militant and criminal factions.

1558453_1558453.caption: Under the pact agreed by President Putin and Viktor Orban Russia will loan 80 of the cost
1558453_1558453.article_context: Hungarian lawmakers have approved a Russian-financed plan to build two new reactors at the country's only nuclear power plant in Paks, backed by a €10 billion loan from Russia. The government asserts that this move will reduce Hungary's reliance on foreign energy sources, but critics warn it will deepen Hungary's dependence on Russia and raise transparency concerns due to the deal's secrecy and lack of a formal bidding process. The European Union has also raised issues regarding fair competition. The agreement has become a key topic ahead of Hungary's general election, with opposition parties and public protests calling for a referendum. The expansion is expected to double the plant's output and create thousands of jobs, though national opinion remains divided.

829582_829582.caption: The eye of Typhoon Maysak category 5 storm as it headed towards the Philippines
829582_829582.article_context: Satellite and aerial images captured several key environmental events around the world. Busy shipping lanes off China and significant dust plumes from West Africa to South America were observed, with Saharan dust providing vital phosphorus to the Amazon rainforest. In the U.S., record-low Sierra Nevada snowpack highlights California's ongoing drought, while the Carrizo Plain's Topaz Solar Farm demonstrates large-scale renewable energy development. Cyclone Pam devastated Vanuatu, causing widespread damage and fatalities. High winds and fires affected southern Chile, London marked increased access to Sentinel satellite data, and other notable events included Arctic solar eclipse imagery, remarkable lightning near Bangkok, ice coverage on the Great Lakes, and volcanic features in the Azores and Hawaii.

974130_974130.caption: Fidel Castro 83 at the National Centre for Scientific Investigation in Havana his first public appearance since 2006
974130_974130.article_context: The Cuban government has begun releasing 52 political prisoners in a move brokered by the Catholic Church, signaling possible steps toward easing tensions with the US. Some of the freed dissidents are expected to go into exile in Spain. This decision follows international pressure after the death of hunger striker Orlando Zapata Tamayo and ongoing protests by relatives of the prisoners. Simultaneously, Fidel Castro appeared in public for the first time in four years, while his brother Raúl has initiated limited reforms since taking power. The releases have been welcomed by the Vatican and US officials, though significant change in US policy, such as lifting the embargo, remains uncertain.

505328_505328.caption: Natalie Bennett on the campaign trail in Norwich
505328_505328.article_context: Natalie Bennett, leader of the Green Party in England and Wales, campaigned in Norwich South as the party experienced a surge in youth support and record membership, aiming to win a second parliamentary seat. Despite increased national backing and attention, doubts persist about the Greens' chances of winning beyond their stronghold in Brighton. Bennett faces scrutiny over party policies and acknowledges the challenges of balancing radical proposals with mainstream appeal. The Greens are focusing their campaign on anti-austerity, climate action, NHS protection, and a Higher minimum wage, while ruling out any coalition deals. Ultimately, Bennett expressed preference for a Labour government under Ed Miliband if forced to choose between the major parties.

1472298_1472298.caption: France has deployed warplanes in Mali
1472298_1472298.article_context: French warplanes launched airstrikes on Gao and other northern towns in Mali, targeting Islamist militants who had seized control of the region. France intervened to halt the militants’ southward advance after they captured the key town of Konna, aiding Malian government forces in recapturing territory. The operation marks a significant escalation, with French ground troops deployed alongside growing support from West African nations and logistical help from the UK, US, and others. French officials stated the Islamists were better equipped and trained than expected, and warned of potential reprisals, particularly given several French hostages are still held by militant groups. The intervention has led to casualties among soldiers and civilians, and prompted mass displacement of local populations.

1647535_1647535.caption: Rand Paul was at the centre of a storm in the US Senate on Sunday night
1647535_1647535.article_context: On Sunday, Senator Rand Paul halted the renewal of key Patriot Act provisions, causing the temporary expiration of the National Security Agency's bulk data collection program. This move, grounded in Paul's libertarian views, won him national attention and support from privacy advocates but also drew criticism from other Republicans, some of whom accused him of prioritizing political ambitions over national security. While this event could boost his standing among younger and independent voters in his presidential campaign, it also risks alienating mainstream party figures and highlights the divisive nature of NSA surveillance within the Republican Party.

300344_300344.caption: USA TODAY s Shannon Rae Green talks with Weather editor Doyle Rice and Politics Editor Paul Singer about whether Obama s historic climate change agreement with China can move forward
300344_300344.article_context: President Obama announced a milestone climate agreement with China, committing the U.S. to cut carbon emissions by 26-28% below 2005 levels by 2025, while China pledged to cap its emissions by 2030. This pact followed months of secret negotiations and was intended to demonstrate leadership from the world’s two largest greenhouse gas emitters ahead of global climate talks. The deal sparked immediate opposition from Congressional Republicans, who criticized its impact on American industry and jobs and vowed to resist related regulations. Despite being non-binding, the agreement is expected to set the stage for executive actions by Obama and to encourage a global climate accord at the Paris conference in 2015.

1448883_1448883.caption: Nicola Sturgeon called for powers over a future referendum should rest with the Scottish Parliament
1448883_1448883.article_context: Nicola Sturgeon, Scotland's incoming first minister, has called for the Scottish Parliament to have permanent authority to call future independence referendums, rather than relying on temporary powers granted by the UK government as in the 2014 vote. While preferring such moves to be made by consensus between Scottish and UK ministers, Sturgeon argued that Holyrood should have the explicit right to decide on referendums. This issue will be considered by the Smith Commission, though it is likely to face resistance from supporters of the Union.

1583944_1583944.caption: Imran Khan was mobbed by supporters as he led a protest march against Nawaz Sharif at the weekend
1583944_1583944.article_context: Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaaf (PTI), the country's second-largest opposition party, has announced it will resign its seats in the national assembly and most provincial assemblies, demanding Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif step down over alleged vote rigging in the 2013 election. Khan and thousands of supporters have staged protests in Islamabad calling for fresh elections, while the government has refused to allow demonstrations in sensitive areas and is unlikely to concede to re-election demands. Concurrently, cleric Tahirul Qadri is leading similar protests for governmental reform, amidst wider dissatisfaction with Pakistan's economy and public services. However, other opposition leaders, including former President Asif Ali Zardari, have criticized the protests and rejected calls for civil disobedience, urging dialogue instead.

1569080_1569080.caption: President Obama together with Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe are the main TPP negotiators
1569080_1569080.article_context: The Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) is set to become the world’s largest and most ambitious free trade deal, involving twelve countries and potentially covering 40% of global trade. The US and Japan are leading the negotiations, focusing on liberalizing sensitive markets, which could set the pace for other members. While Japan expects significant economic gains and strategic benefits, there is debate about China’s exclusion, with experts suggesting that China’s participation would bring both economic and reputational advantages. Vietnam stands to benefit most from increased apparel exports to the US at zero tariffs, though it faces challenges over rules of origin and state enterprise reforms. The TPP’s success could reshape trade dynamics in the Asia-Pacific region and influence future global economic policies.

1182455_1182455.caption: David Cameron speaks during PMQs on Wednesday when he revealed he intervened to help Cotswold Wildlife Park import a rhino
1182455_1182455.article_context: Prime Minister David Cameron pledged government support to help the Isle of Wight zoo import a rescued tiger currently held in isolation in Belgium, after the issue was raised in Parliament. The tiger, originally a circus animal, has been in a Belgian rescue centre for two years due to bureaucratic delays. Government agencies will now work with the zoo to ensure proper procedures are followed for the transfer. The zoo's director and supporters welcomed the unexpected political backing, emphasizing the animal's welfare and its potential as an ambassador for conservation.

127158_127158.caption: Hillary Clinton campaigns in San Diego on Thursday
127158_127158.article_context: Everytown for Gun Safety, a major gun violence prevention group backed by Michael Bloomberg, has endorsed Hillary Clinton for president, citing her consistent support for tougher gun laws and background checks. The group, which includes Moms Demand Action and other advocacy networks, chose Clinton over Bernie Sanders due to her stronger commitment to gun control. This endorsement comes soon after the NRA endorsed Donald Trump, highlighting a clear divide between the candidates on gun policy. Although Bloomberg founded the group, he has not personally endorsed any candidate.

1493067_1493067.caption: Marea in April 2015 after a car bombing thought to have been carried out by Islamic State
1493067_1493067.article_context: An old photo of a Syrian amateur football team from the 1980s inspired a journalist to track the fate of its members amid Syria's devastating civil war. The 13 men, once united by sport in the town of Marea, have been scattered by political upheaval, violence, and displacement. Some have fled abroad or become refugees, others remain amidst ongoing bombings and siege, with careers ranging from fighting in rebel groups to trading across conflict lines and serving as mayor in contested territories. Though all survived, their lives have been shaped by separation, loss, and the enduring effects of war, making a reunion on the pitch unlikely.

541002_541002.caption: Shinzo Abe bows to Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko during a national memorial service for the victims of the 2011 earthquake and tsunami
541002_541002.article_context: Rising tensions between Japan and China over the disputed Senkaku islands have brought international attention to Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, whose conservative and nationalist stance is seen by critics as provocative but by supporters as a sign of Japan finally standing up for itself. Since returning to power in 2012, Abe has avoided overtly confrontational actions with China while focusing on revitalizing Japan's economy through 'Abenomics' and expanding Japan's global influence, including closer ties with Southeast Asia and securing the 2020 Olympics. His administration remains popular domestically, but his efforts to reinterpret Japan's pacifist constitution and address historical issues continue to spark regional controversy. The unresolved question is how Abe will respond if tensions with China escalate further.

386978_386978.caption: Hillary Clinton delivers remarks at a primary night campaign event on April 26 2016 in Philadelphia
386978_386978.article_context: Hillary Clinton won the Democratic primaries in Pennsylvania, Maryland, Connecticut, and Delaware, solidifying her lead and making it nearly impossible for Bernie Sanders to capture the nomination. Sanders, however, won Rhode Island and vowed to continue his campaign through to the convention, emphasizing his progressive platform and ongoing enthusiasm among supporters. Clinton shifted her focus to uniting the Democratic Party and preparing for a general election against Republican frontrunner Donald Trump, while Sanders maintained his criticisms of the political establishment. After Tuesday’s results, Clinton was expected to have about 90% of the delegates needed to secure the nomination.

176015_176015.caption: Israeli troops look through a damaged window after a rocket landed nearby killing an Israeli civilian last week on the IsraelGaza border
176015_176015.article_context: Nathan J. Brown debunks five common misconceptions about Hamas, arguing that while the group cannot defeat Israel militarily, it still poses a significant threat by making Israelis feel vulnerable and forcing political responses. He asserts that Hamas’s popularity is not mainly due to its social services but stems from its image as an unyielding, uncorrupted resistance force, despite declining public support and electoral prospects. Recent losses of regional allies have reduced Hamas’s resources and diplomatic options, but relinquishing government control in Gaza has given the group more flexibility to pursue armed resistance. Finally, Brown contends that although Hamas is resilient and committed to its cause, it lacks a clear, effective strategy to achieve its overarching goals for Palestine.

122621_122621.caption: Virginia delegates Hala Ayala left and Eileen Filler celebrate the nomination of Kaine as vice president
122621_122621.article_context: At the Democratic National Convention, Vice President Joe Biden delivered a passionate speech endorsing Hillary Clinton for president, emphasizing her empathy and experience as a champion for the middle class and working families. He contrasted Clinton’s qualifications and compassion with Donald Trump’s lack of understanding of the middle class, criticizing Trump's rhetoric and perceived unfitness for national security leadership. Biden also praised President Obama’s character, invoked his own personal experiences with loss, and called for unity and optimism about America’s future, urging voters to reject fear and division.

1464180_1464180.caption: David Cameron s EU referendum promise was a votewinner with the public but now he has to face his party
1464180_1464180.article_context: Amid Labour’s visible internal divisions, the Conservative Party faces its own growing conflict over Britain’s EU membership, highlighted by tensions around the upcoming EU referendum. The party’s history of splitting over core issues, like the Corn Laws and EU membership, threatens party unity as the 2017 referendum approaches. Prime Minister David Cameron’s credibility is at stake; if he campaigns to remain in the EU, he risks attacks from party members who favor leaving. This leadership struggle could intensify after the referendum regardless of the result, potentially corroding Tory unity further and impacting the future structure of UK political parties.

96424_96424.caption: Art Walker then 74 was injured in a 2015 road rage incident in Montgomery County
96424_96424.article_context: Art Walker, a 74-year-old retiree, was violently assaulted by 26-year-old Ryan Wallace after a road rage incident in Montgomery County, Maryland. Following prolonged tailgating, Wallace confronted Walker at a stoplight, punched him, and caused serious injuries that required extended hospitalization and rehabilitation. Wallace was convicted of second-degree assault and sentenced to six years in prison, a term exceeding state guidelines. Walker has mostly recovered but says the attack left lasting impacts on his health and daily life.

1565137_1565137.caption: GM did not say whether the Cruze sales halt would apply to markets outside the US
1565137_1565137.article_context: General Motors announced the recall of an additional 824,000 cars from model years 2008-2011 due to a defect in ignition switches that can cause engines to shut off and disable airbags, raising the total number of vehicles affected by this issue to over 2 million. This flaw has been linked to at least 12 deaths, though some reports suggest the number may be much higher. GM also halted sales of certain Chevrolet Cruze models for unrelated reasons. The company faces two congressional investigations over delays in the initial recall and CEO Mary Barra is scheduled to testify about GM's handling of the issue.

440738_440738.caption: President Barack Obama delivers the State of the Union address
440738_440738.article_context: In his State of the Union address, President Obama acknowledged past unfulfilled promises by previous presidents and positioned his own proposals—such as raising the capital gains tax and increasing tax credits for working families—as a foundation for ongoing debate about broadening the benefits of economic recovery to the middle class. Despite facing a Republican-controlled Congress and recent Democratic electoral losses, Obama emphasized that the U.S. economy had stabilized and called for policies promoting shared prosperity. The speech was less a detailed legislative agenda and more a thematic appeal for economic fairness, delivered amid continued partisan divisions in Washington.

1544140_1544140.caption: Danny Swanson was attacked after leaving a restaurant on Glasgow s Queen Street
1544140_1544140.article_context: A Dundee United football player, Danny Swanson, was hospitalized after being knocked unconscious during a late-night brawl in Glasgow city centre in November 2010. The incident occurred when Swanson, along with teammates, was attacked by John Friel, who punched him on the head. During the same altercation, ex-Dundee United youth player Matthew Flynn head butted Barry Douglas and assaulted a passer-by, John Stuart, who tried to help Swanson. Both Friel and Flynn admitted to assault charges in Glasgow Sheriff Court, and sentencing was deferred.

459656_459656.caption: A photograph of Lee Rigby of the Royal Regiment of Fusiliers at the field of remembrance at Westminster Abbey in London
459656_459656.article_context: An official report examining how much the security services knew about the extremists who murdered soldier Lee Rigby in 2013 will be released next week. The report, from parliament's intelligence and security committee, has already been delivered to Prime Minister David Cameron, with a public version to follow. One of the attackers, Michael Adebolajo, was previously known to authorities. Both attackers are serving life sentences. The government is also planning to introduce new counter-terrorism measures in response.

126976_126976.caption: Donald Trump speaks during a campaign stop at the Signature Flight Hangar at Port Columbus International Airport in Columbus Ohio on March 1
126976_126976.article_context: Todd Stern, who led U.S. negotiations on the Paris climate agreement, refutes Donald Trump’s claim that the accord allows foreign bureaucrats to control American energy use. Stern explains that the agreement lets each country set its own emission reduction plans, with no external authority over national policies. He warns that Trump’s pledge to withdraw from the Paris Agreement is both misguided and impossible to cancel for all countries, as the U.S. could only remove itself. Stern argues that leaving the agreement would undermine global efforts against climate change and damage U.S. diplomatic standing.

44386_44386.caption: NOAA flies over the Arctic this fall to measure sea ice coverage The extent of sea ice in September 2014 was the sixth lowest since satellite observations began in 1979
44386_44386.article_context: A recent Yale study reveals that while moderate and liberal Republicans widely acknowledge climate change and support related policies like emissions limits and regulating carbon dioxide, they make up only a small fraction of the party, with conservatives and tea party members comprising the majority and opposing these measures. Climate change is also not a priority concern for most Republicans, especially during primary season when the party's most conservative voters dominate. However, younger Republicans show more openness to environmental action, suggesting party views could shift in the future, even though significant change appears unlikely for now.

986143_986143.caption: Pakistani security personnel and volunteers carry injured blast victims after the suicide bomb attack in Quetta
986143_986143.article_context: Suicide bombers targeted the deputy chief of the Frontier Corps in Quetta, western Pakistan, killing 23 people—including eight soldiers and the officer’s wife—in a coordinated assault. The attack occurred shortly after Pakistani authorities arrested a senior al-Qaida operative in the city, raising suspicions that Taliban militants were behind the bombing. The incident highlights ongoing instability in Balochistan, a region known as a base for both Taliban and al-Qaida fighters, and follows increased pressure on militant groups due to recent high-profile arrests and drone strikes.

117707_117707.caption: Violent clashes erupt at Trump campaign events in Tuscon but they re nothing new
117707_117707.article_context: The Republican Party's 2016 presidential campaign is marked by deep divisions, with key candidates abandoning a previous loyalty pledge to support the eventual GOP nominee. Donald Trump, the frontrunner, has disrupted the party’s stability and faces strong opposition from establishment Republicans and rival candidates Ted Cruz and John Kasich. During a CNN town hall, all three withdrew their support for the pledge, highlighting the fracturing coalition and uncertainty in the party. Cruz hopes to defeat Trump in key states like Wisconsin, while Kasich relies on a potential brokered convention. The GOP faces possible internal chaos whether Trump is nominated or denied, as party unity unravels and concerns grow about the upcoming convention and general election.

923315_923315.caption: UN analysts will present a report showing that environmental damage such as BP s Deepwater Horizon spill is bad for business at a symposium this week
923315_923315.article_context: UN environmental leader Pavan Sukhdev warns that modern businesses risk becoming destructive 'soulless corporations' due to their short-term approach to environmental issues, lobbying against policies to protect nature, and failing to account for ecosystem damage. Ahead of publishing his major report, The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity for Business, Sukhdev urges greater societal regulation of corporate behavior. The report estimates global forest destruction costs economies trillions annually and highlights disasters like the BP oil spill as examples of corporate harm. Sukhdev argues the benefits of environmental protection far outweigh the costs, recommending businesses report their environmental impacts alongside financial results and advocating for stricter limits on extraction and pollution.

178798_178798.caption: Plainclothes police detain a suspect after an attempted suicide bombing at St Yoseph Catholic Church in Medan Indonesia
178798_178798.article_context: An attacker inspired by ISIS attempted to bomb a crowded church in Medan, Indonesia, but the device failed to detonate and only burst into flames. The attacker, armed with a bomb and an ax, managed to slightly injure a priest before being subdued by churchgoers and arrested by police. This incident marks the second ISIS-inspired attack in Indonesia this year, reflecting growing concerns about the group's influence in the country. Authorities are investigating the suspect's possible connections to other militants, while the government has taken steps to strengthen anti-terrorism laws in response to rising threats.

1183056_1183056.caption: A fire salamander infected by the skineating fungal disease which experts believe has been exported from Asia to Europe by the exotic pet trade
1183056_1183056.article_context: A deadly skin-eating fungus originating in Southeast Asia, Batrachochytrium salamandrivorans, has spread to Europe through the exotic pet trade and now threatens to wipe out native amphibian species, especially the endangered great crested newt in the UK. While Asian salamanders are immune, European and American newts and salamanders have no resistance, putting them at extreme risk. The fungus recently caused a massive die-off of fire salamanders in the Netherlands. Scientists warn that stricter controls and biosecurity measures are needed to prevent further spread, as global trade in exotic amphibians continues to facilitate transmission. UK officials remain vigilant but report that the fungus is not yet present in the country.

1668820_1668820.caption: Relations between the central government in Dushanbe and the mountainous region of Badakhshan have always been difficult
1668820_1668820.article_context: Alexander Sodiqov, a Tajik academic working on a UK-funded research project about conflict management in Central Asia, was detained by security forces in Tajikistan’s Gorno-Badakhshan region on suspicion of espionage. Supporters are urging the British government to intervene for his release, while Amnesty International and Reporters Without Borders have condemned his arrest as a threat to intellectual freedom. Media reports suggest he may face treason charges with a possible 20-year prison sentence, raising concerns about academic freedom and fair legal treatment amidst regional tensions and unrest.

259318_259318.caption: An Israeli airstrike in Rafah Gaza sends debris and smoke into the sky
259318_259318.article_context: Israel and Hamas have agreed to a 72-hour cease-fire in Gaza, set to begin Tuesday morning, allowing Israeli ground troops to withdraw after completing their mission to destroy 32 militant tunnels. The cease-fire, brokered by Egypt, aims to enable indirect negotiations for a longer-term agreement, though previous truces have quickly failed. The conflict, which began on July 8, has resulted in heavy casualties, with over 1,880 Palestinians and more than 60 Israeli soldiers killed. Despite the temporary halt in fighting, sporadic violence continues, including a suspected terrorist attack in Jerusalem involving a construction vehicle and a separate shooting of an Israeli soldier. The truce comes amid rising international pressure on Israel over civilian deaths in Gaza.

271963_271963.caption: Volunteer Muneo Kanno stands near a radiation meter in front of the Iitate Town Hall on Feb 25 2015
271963_271963.article_context: Four years after the 2011 earthquake, tsunami, and subsequent meltdown at the Fukushima Dai-ichi nuclear plant, thousands of Japanese evacuees, including residents of Iitate village, remain unable to return home due to persistent radiation. Despite extensive cleanup and some progress in decommissioning the plant, much of the region remains off-limits, and many evacuees are reluctant to return due to mistrust and concerns over lingering contamination. Housing shortages, slow recovery efforts, and uncertainty about long-term safety contribute to ongoing displacement, with experts predicting it may take decades before normal life can resume in the affected areas.

1626584_1626584.caption: President Maduro says that more than a third of subsidised goods are smuggled out of Venezuela
1626584_1626584.article_context: Venezuela's annual inflation rate has reached 63.4%, making it the highest in Latin America, according to newly released official data. The government has faced criticism for previously withholding economic figures, and continues to struggle with severe shortages of basic goods. President Nicolas Maduro’s administration has blamed recent anti-government protests for the economic turmoil, although international economists attribute the crisis to government policies and controls. Widespread smuggling of subsidized goods into Colombia remains a major issue, prompting nighttime border closures and the arrest of hundreds of people. Economic forecasts predict a further contraction of Venezuela’s GDP and warn of a possible deeper recession and default.

347220_347220.caption: A Syrian army tank rolls through in Qusair on June 5 The Syrian army has captured the strategic town near the Lebanese border solidifying recent gains against rebel forces
347220_347220.article_context: Syrian government forces, supported by Hezbollah fighters, captured the strategic city of al-Qusayr near the Lebanese border, forcing Syrian rebels and wounded civilians to retreat after heavy bombardment and dwindling supplies. The loss marks a significant blow to the opposition, cutting off key supply routes and strengthening the regime’s position both regionally and in its alliance with Hezbollah. The battle’s aftermath has deepened divisions within Syria’s opposition, raised fears of civilian massacres, and sparked international concern, with Russia vetoing UN intervention. The fall of al-Qusayr is seen as a turning point in the Syrian conflict, impacting both the military balance and the morale of anti-Assad forces.

1504537_1504537.caption: Wednesday s emergency summit in Brussels will also focus on tightening EU borders and boosting aid to neighbours of Syria
1504537_1504537.article_context: European Union leaders met in Brussels to approve a plan to relocate 120,000 migrants among member states, revealing significant East-West divisions over mandatory quotas. Western countries, led by Germany, are pushing for solidarity, while Eastern states express strong opposition and feel their sovereignty is threatened. Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban, previously isolated, is now influencing regional resistance to accepting refugees. Critics question the effectiveness and fairness of the quota system, warning it could deepen rifts within the EU. Some voices highlight the need for migration to address demographic challenges, but public opinion in several Eastern countries remains firmly against taking in refugees.

59746_59746.caption: This undated photo provided by WDBJTV shows Vester Lee Flanagan II who killed WDBJ reporter Alison Parker and cameraman Adam Ward on Wednesday
59746_59746.article_context: After a disgruntled former employee killed two journalists on live TV in Virginia, Governor Terry McAuliffe expressed support for making it easier for employers to share personnel records, arguing that such information could help prevent workplace violence. He also reiterated his push to close the gun show loophole in Virginia, though he acknowledged stricter background checks cannot prevent all shootings. The discussion took place on a radio program, where McAuliffe responded to questions about both the shooting and the state's handling of law enforcement personnel files, including a separate controversy about releasing a report on a violent police arrest.

1562486_1562486.caption: Lib Dem Geoff Juby got 349 votes at the Rochester and Strood byelection
1562486_1562486.article_context: Many candidates stand in 'safe seats' during general elections despite having little chance of winning, driven by motives such as gaining experience, representing alternative viewpoints, or using it as a stepping stone in politics. Experts note that party support is usually minimal and the experience can be isolating, yet some prominent politicians began their careers in this way. Despite the near certainty of defeat, candidates value the opportunity to participate in the democratic process and gain exposure, with some reporting positive experiences even when heavily outnumbered by the incumbent party.

142995_142995.caption: Mitt Romney and running mate Paul Ryan part ways at Denver International Airport in Colorado
142995_142995.article_context: Mitt Romney held his final rally before Election Day in Manchester, New Hampshire, addressing a crowd of 12,000 supporters at an energetic event featuring music from Kid Rock. In his remarks, Romney emphasized the momentum behind his campaign and called for a new beginning for America. Ann Romney also spoke, reflecting on their campaign journey and expressing hope for the country's future. The rally highlighted Romney's focus on securing support in the critical battleground state as voting approached.

933040_933040.caption: The strike comes just weeks after Foxconn was forced to close a plant in Taiyuan
933040_933040.article_context: Thousands of Foxconn workers in China went on strike at the Zhengzhou factory, disrupting iPhone 5 production, in protest against strict quality controls imposed by Foxconn and Apple without adequate training. The strike was further fueled by workers being forced to work during a public holiday and unresolved conflicts between staff and management. The walkout reflects growing worker unrest and highlights concerns over labor conditions at Apple's supplier factories.

805875_805875.caption: David Cameron lays out his party s pledge on taxation during a visit to an engineering factory in Birmingham
805875_805875.article_context: Prime Minister David Cameron has announced a five-year 'tax lock,' promising legislation to prevent any increases to income tax, VAT, or national insurance before May 2020 if the Conservatives win the general election. While Cameron claims the pledge is possible based on current fiscal plans, leading economists and critics argue that such legislation would severely limit the government's financial flexibility, especially in times of economic crisis, and could easily be reversed by future parliamentary action. Opposition parties, including Labour, the Liberal Democrats, and UKIP, dismissed the move as a political gimmick, questioning its credibility and suggesting the Conservatives may instead make cuts elsewhere, such as to welfare or tax credits.

1556473_1556473.caption: Tom Brake now the only Lib Dem MP in London on the campaign trail with Nick Clegg
1556473_1556473.article_context: Nick Clegg resigned as leader of the Liberal Democrats following a devastating election result, which saw the party's representation in Parliament drop from 57 to just eight MPs. Several prominent Lib Dem figures, including Vince Cable and Danny Alexander, lost their seats. Key survivors such as Tim Farron, Norman Lamb, Greg Mulholland, John Pugh, Mark Williams, Alistair Carmichael, and Tom Brake retained their positions, though most saw reduced majorities. A leadership election has been called as the party faces a period of reflection and rebuilding, with some MPs ruling themselves out of the leadership race.

848430_848430.caption: Members of the Donbas volunteer battalion take part in exercises in their camp on the border between Dnipropetrovsk and Donetsk regions
848430_848430.article_context: In eastern Ukraine, volunteer battalions such as the Donbas and Dnepr units have emerged to support government forces in their struggle against pro-Russia separatists. Made up of largely untrained volunteers, these irregular militias have played a significant role due to the reluctance of some professional soldiers to fight, often operating under minimal coordination and training. Tensions and violence have escalated, with incidents of civilian casualties in cities like Mariupol fuelling further anger and propaganda. The involvement of far-right elements and lack of discipline within some battalions have raised additional concerns, while both the Ukrainian and separatist sides consist of fragmented groups with conflicting interests and growing animosity. The situation risks spiralling into uncontrolled conflict, reminiscent of other civil wars.

257611_257611.caption: Chinese workers are silhouetted against the smog in Beijing on Dec 1 2015 Beijing issued an orange alert for heavy smog Nov 30 2015 the highest level this year
257611_257611.article_context: Beijing experienced its fifth straight day of severe smog, prompting authorities to close schools and recommend students study from home due to hazardous air quality. The pollution, far exceeding safe levels, caused health concerns among parents and forced highway closures. This crisis coincided with President Xi Jinping's participation in a global climate change summit, where he pledged to reduce China's emissions—the highest in the world. Despite efforts like stricter standards and investment in renewables, China still relies heavily on coal, and officials say significant improvements in air quality may take five to ten years.

83587_83587.caption: Russian bombers use airbase in Iran to strike targets in Syria
83587_83587.article_context: Russian bombers launched airstrikes in Syria from an Iranian air base for the first time, demonstrating deepening military cooperation between Russia and Iran and expanding Russia's presence in the Middle East. The strikes targeted rebel-held areas in Syrian provinces, mainly hitting opposition forces to President Bashar al-Assad rather than terrorist groups. This move marks a significant shift in the regional dynamics, as Iran traditionally opposes foreign military bases on its territory. The operation allows Russia to intensify its air campaign due to closer proximity, while U.S. officials expressed concern over the impact on an already complex Syrian conflict. Human rights organizations criticized Russia and Syria for civilian casualties, alleging the use of banned incendiary weapons.

1571827_1571827.caption: Mr Cameron headed to Scotland when he feared the Union was in peril
