Furthermore, Facebook has changed how news is both distributed and consumed, with more users relying on it as a primary source of information. The platform continues to evolve, shaping and reflecting societal changes worldwide.

803337_803337.caption: Prince Philip Prince William Prince Harry Earl Spencer and Prince Charles walk together behind the carriage carrying the casket of Princess Diana
803337_803337.article_context: Alastair Campbell’s diaries reveal that St James’s Palace feared for Prince Charles’s safety during Diana’s funeral procession and believed he could face public attack unless his sons walked with him behind Diana’s coffin. The diaries detail internal debates about how to handle the funeral, including Prince William’s strong resentment towards the media and resistance to participating. They also describe Prime Minister Tony Blair’s tense relations with Prince Charles and Chancellor Gordon Brown, including Margaret Thatcher’s warning about Brown’s attitude and Campbell’s own role in spreading claims about Brown’s 'psychological flaws.' The extracts highlight the royal family’s concern about public perception following Diana’s death and their pressured response to media criticism.

570812_570812.caption: Striking French sailors on an emergency boat in Marseille
570812_570812.article_context: Major protests erupted across France as high school students and workers united against the government's proposed pension and retirement reforms. Demonstrations included blockading school entrances and fuel depots, setting up barricades at oil refineries, and confrontations with police in cities like Paris, Lyon, Marseille, and Bordeaux. The widespread unrest saw mayors and union leaders speaking out in support, highlighting significant public opposition to the reforms.

138192_138192.caption: Factchecking the ninth Democratic debate
138192_138192.article_context: During the ninth Democratic presidential debate hosted by CNN, key factual disputes arose between Hillary Clinton and Bernie Sanders on trade agreements, gun control, campaign contributions, and other issues. Fact-checking revealed that Sanders’s claim that Clinton supported nearly all major trade deals was accurate, though the job-loss impact was disputed. Clinton was found to have misrepresented Vermont’s role in New York crime guns and overstated her support for a $15 federal minimum wage. Both candidates engaged in misleading attacks regarding financial industry regulation and fossil fuel contributions. On fracking, Sanders correctly asserted Clinton’s active promotion abroad. Sanders’s stance on allowing Sandy Hook families to sue gun manufacturers has shifted during the campaign. Sanders exaggerated U.S. spending on NATO, and both campaigns have overstated their fundraising claims and election vote counts. Clinton’s claim about GOP efforts to privatize Social Security also lacked full context. Fact-checkers highlighted the complexity and nuance often omitted in debate statements.

1648496_1648496.caption: As a Russian MP Andrei Lugovoi wanted by UK police has immunity from prosecution
1648496_1648496.article_context: Alexei Torubarov, a former businessman from Volgograd, Russia, claims to be targeted by the Kremlin due to his opposition to corruption and association with anti-Putin figures. Accused of fraud by Russian authorities, Torubarov fled the country and experienced imprisonment, an assassination attempt, and repeated extradition efforts. After seeking asylum in Hungary, his application was twice denied over 'national security reasons,' despite concerns by human rights groups that returning him to Russia could put him at risk. Torubarov's case highlights the political and diplomatic tensions around asylum seekers facing charges widely believed to be politically motivated.

1598096_1598096.caption: Taiwan first authorised the sale of a GM animal as a pet
1598096_1598096.article_context: Scientists are close to receiving final approval from US regulators to produce AquAdvantage, a genetically modified Atlantic salmon that grows to full size in half the normal time, the first GM animal potentially fit for human consumption. While developers claim the fish are sterile and securely farmed, concerns remain about possible ecological impacts should they escape into the wild. The article also highlights other genetically modified animals, such as fluorescent fish sold as pets and livestock engineered to resist disease, raising broader ethical debates over genetic modification for food, medicine, and the environment.

211008_211008.caption: The black boxes of a Libyan Afriqiyah Airways passenger plane
211008_211008.article_context: In response to the disappearance of Malaysia Airlines Flight 370, Rep. David Price urged the adoption of ejectable flight recorders on commercial planes to make crash investigations easier and faster. He highlighted that such technology has been recommended since 9/11 and is already used in military aircraft. Transportation Secretary Anthony Foxx said the FAA is studying the benefits and costs of the proposal. The recorders, which eject and float after crashes, could potentially reduce time-consuming and expensive search efforts following accidents over water or in remote areas.

103634_103634.caption: Iman alObaidi is seen in Tripoli in this Saturday March 26 2011 file photo after storming into a hotel s breakfast room to show her wounds to foreign media
103634_103634.article_context: Iman al-Obaidi, a Libyan woman who accused Gaddafi loyalists of rape, was forcibly deported from Qatar to rebel-held eastern Libya against her will, despite her fears for her safety and objections. The U.N. expressed grave concern for her future and security, and noted that Obaidi had faced hostility both from Libyan government officials and rebels, as well as threats. Separately, at least 200 migrants went missing after their boat sank off Tunisia while trying to cross from Libya to Europe, with hundreds rescued.

242261_242261.caption: Oscar Pistorius arrives at court in Pretoria South Africa on June 30
242261_242261.article_context: Oscar Pistorius, the double-amputee Olympian accused of killing his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp, was found by two mental health reports to not be suffering from any mental illness at the time of the shooting, according to his prosecutor. The court resumed after a month-long break for psychological evaluation, and the findings indicated Pistorius was capable of understanding the wrongfulness of his actions. Pistorius claims he shot Steenkamp by accident, mistaking her for an intruder, while prosecutors allege it was the result of a quarrel. The trial continues with expert testimony regarding Pistorius' disability and its relevance to the case.

1639333_1639333.caption: Opec may be attempting to force highercost American shale frackers out of business
1639333_1639333.article_context: Global oil prices have plunged below $50 per barrel, a historically low point compared to their previous peak of over $145 just seven years ago, highlighting the commodity's notorious volatility. This fall benefits oil-importing countries like India and Japan while threatening oil-dependent governments such as Russia, Iran, and Venezuela. In Britain, there are more gainers than losers, but the North Sea oil industry and Scotland’s economy are particularly vulnerable due to rising production costs, mature fields, and decreasing output. The downturn also puts pressure on the UK Treasury to introduce tax incentives and on policymakers to improve infrastructure and skills in affected regions. Experts warn politicians to lower their expectations for future tax revenues from oil, as the industry's profitability and tax contributions are now much less certain.

1207038_1207038.caption: Russia s president Vladimir Putin trying to change the rules of the net
1207038_1207038.article_context: The upcoming World Conference on International Telecommunications (WCIT-12) in Dubai, organized by the ITU, has sparked concerns about potential efforts by authoritarian regimes like Russia, China, and Iran to push for increased state control over the internet through secretive negotiations. Critics argue that the ITU's closed, government-dominated process is unsuitable for regulating the global internet and could threaten internet freedom by enabling state censorship and control. While some see the likelihood of sweeping changes as remote, leaked documents show that proposed treaty amendments could support national initiatives to create tightly controlled internet spaces and restrict online privacy and political activity. The secrecy of the negotiations has intensified these concerns, highlighting the risks of allowing the ITU to play a larger role in internet governance.

1639086_1639086.caption: Most of the Golan Heights were captured by Israel from Syria and occupied ever since Israeli tanks are seen on manoeuvres here in 1991
1639086_1639086.article_context: On Yom Kippur in 1973, Egypt and Syria launched a surprise attack on Israel, aiming to reclaim territories lost in the 1967 war and restore national pride. Initially successful, their advances were reversed after three weeks of intense fighting, and the war concluded with a ceasefire. The conflict involved Cold War powers, with Russia supporting Arab nations and the US backing Israel. Its far-reaching impact included global fuel shortages after Arab oil exporters reduced supply to punish the West, sparking an economic downturn. Diplomatically, Egypt eventually shifted allegiance to the United States and regained Sinai through peace talks, while the war reset military and political attitudes in the region and highlighted the continuing instability in the Middle East.

221534_221534.caption: ProRussian activists and Crimean Tatar protesters and supporters of Maydan stand opposite each other near the Parliament building in Simferopol Crimea Ukraine Feb 26 2014
221534_221534.article_context: Dozens of heavily armed pro-Russia gunmen seized government buildings in Crimea, raising the Russian flag and escalating tensions in Ukraine after the ousting of pro-Russian President Yanukovych. Ukraine responded by placing domestic security forces on high alert and warned Russia against military aggression. Russia began large-scale military exercises involving 150,000 troops near the Ukrainian border, prompting international concerns and warnings from the U.S. The seizure in Crimea, a region with deep ties to Russia and strategic importance, highlighted the growing divide between pro-Russian and pro-Western forces in Ukraine during a period of significant political turmoil.

198867_198867.caption: McConnell in 2008 Senate should not stop confirming judges in election year
198867_198867.article_context: The article examines accusations of hypocrisy among top senators—Chuck Schumer, Mitch McConnell, and Patrick Leahy—regarding election-year Supreme Court nominations. After Justice Scalia’s death, McConnell said the Senate should delay filling the vacancy until after the next presidential election, blocking any Obama nominee. The piece highlights how each senator has flip-flopped or shifted their position over the years: Schumer once suggested blocking Bush’s nominees except in ‘extraordinary circumstances,’ McConnell criticized the idea of stopping confirmations during an election year in 2008 but now supports it, and Leahy previously invoked the so-called ‘Thurmond Rule’ but recently dismissed its validity. The article concludes that all three have changed their stances on Supreme Court nominations in presidential election years, emphasizing the partisan nature of the debate.

1683329_1683329.caption: David Cameron and George Osborne visited Morecambe during the election campaign
1683329_1683329.article_context: Labour is grappling with the aftermath of a severe electoral defeat, having lost key seats and fallen to its lowest number of MPs since 1987. In battleground constituencies like Bury North, Labour narrowly lost to the Conservatives, despite increasing its vote share in the North West overall. Key factors cited for Labour's poor performance include ineffective campaign strategies, lack of trust in Ed Miliband's leadership, and the party’s diminished credibility on the economy. Many traditional Labour voters turned to UKIP, expressing disillusionment and a sense that Labour was out of touch with their concerns. As the party searches for a new leader, there is a consensus among members and analysts that Labour must redefine its vision and better address the needs of disaffected voters to regain support.

1574400_1574400.caption: Nigerian soldiers have retaken many towns from Boko Haram in a recent offensive
1574400_1574400.article_context: Nigeria's military imposed a 24-hour curfew in Maiduguri after Boko Haram militants launched a surprise attack, marking their most serious attempt to re-enter the city since the army reclaimed urban areas in March. Streets emptied and essential services closed as troops and vigilantes repelled the attackers, with reports of casualties on both sides, including deaths from suicide bombings. The army stated that the situation is under control and the curfew aims to protect residents while highlighting ongoing security concerns despite previous gains against Boko Haram.

1633628_1633628.caption: A trader in Mumbai China s dramatic drop is largely down to fears that the rate its economy is growing could be slowing more than thought
1633628_1633628.article_context: On Black Monday, China's Shanghai Composite index plunged 8.5%, marking its most severe decline since 2007 and sparking global market turmoil. The sharp fall reflected widespread fear and uncertainty among traders and investors, triggering international concern about the health of China's economy and its impact on global financial markets.

296556_296556.caption: Apple s shares are lagging the market ahead of the iPhone 7 launch
296556_296556.article_context: Apple's latest iPhone launch was met with less investor enthusiasm compared to previous years, with the stock barely rising before the announcement and only slightly increasing on launch day. This muted reaction reflects concerns about slowing revenue growth and market maturity for the iPhone, which remains Apple's key product. While rivals like Samsung have gained ground, particularly with strong Galaxy S7 sales, Apple continues to dominate premium smartphone profits. Analysts expect modest gains in Apple's stock and revenue in the coming year, but the company faces challenges due to slower growth and underperforming non-iPhone products.

1606782_1606782.caption: Links between the Paris and Brussels bombers
1606782_1606782.article_context: Brussels airport will take months to fully reopen after being targeted by Islamist bombers, with reconstruction needed throughout the building. Attempts to resume partial services have been delayed, and enhanced security measures are being introduced. Thirty-two people died in the attacks, which were claimed by ISIS, and dozens remain hospitalized. Authorities continue to hunt for suspects, with several arrests made across Europe. Questions and criticism have emerged regarding the handling of suspects and the roots of extremism in Brussels and Paris.

226424_226424.caption: Paul is joined by his wife Kelley to announce the start of his presidential campaign on April 7 2015 at the Galt House Hotel in Louisville Ky
226424_226424.article_context: Sen. Rand Paul of Kentucky released a campaign video positioning himself as a 'different kind of Republican' ahead of announcing his 2016 presidential run. The video emphasizes his libertarian views, outreach to minority voters, devotion to constitutional principles, and past filibuster against the CIA director nomination. Paul will officially enter the GOP race during a rally in Louisville, then campaign in early primary states, joining Sen. Ted Cruz as an official candidate and competing with other prominent Republicans for the nomination.

161296_161296.caption: The Canadarm 2 reaches out to capture the SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft for docking to the International Space Station
161296_161296.article_context: The investigation into the recent SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket explosion at Cape Canaveral took a notable turn when a SpaceX employee requested access to a United Launch Alliance (ULA) building's roof—prompted by suspicious imagery seen during the probe. Although ULA denied access and called Air Force investigators, no evidence of sabotage was found. SpaceX, which leads the investigation with government agencies' support, continues to assess all possible causes, including sabotage, but has focused on a breach in the rocket's helium system. The incident has intensified the rivalry between SpaceX and ULA over lucrative government contracts, and some lawmakers have called for SpaceX to relinquish control of the investigation to federal authorities. Despite unresolved questions, SpaceX aims to resume launches, though industry skepticism remains regarding its timeline.

800329_800329.caption: An Iraqi soldier in the Jurf alSakher area about 50km south of Baghdad protects the region from further Isis gains after the fall of Ramadi
800329_800329.article_context: Senior military officials from Britain and the US have criticized the Iraqi army for lacking the motivation and leadership needed to resist advances by Islamic State militants, despite being numerically superior. Following the fall of Ramadi to ISIS, US Defense Secretary Ash Carter stated that Iraqi forces showed 'no will to fight,' a sentiment echoed by Maj Gen Tim Cross who attributed the military’s setbacks to poor moral cohesion and ineffective command. Iraqi leaders and Iranian officials rejected these claims, blaming inadequate US support. The discussion has prompted calls for reassessment of international strategy, but experts argue that external military assistance alone cannot resolve the deeper problems within Iraq’s armed forces.

393841_393841.caption: Watch what happens when Michael Goodman says sorry for the crap he put Claude Soffel through
393841_393841.article_context: Michael Goodman, who mugged Claude Soffel 35 years ago, reconnected with his victim on Facebook decades later. Goodman confessed to his past crime in an online exchange, leading to an unexpected reconciliation between the two men after many years.

114878_114878.caption: Kurdish security forces take up positions as they attack Islamic Statecontrolled villages surrounding Mosul on Monday
114878_114878.article_context: The battle to reclaim Mosul from the Islamic State began with a major offensive led by Iraqi Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi. Iraqi forces, supported by a U.S.-led coalition, Kurdish peshmerga, and potentially Shiite militias, are advancing on the city, where more than a million civilians remain trapped. The complex coalition, while united against ISIS, faces internal tensions that could lead to further conflict, as rival groups struggle over power and land. Only specific Iraqi forces are allowed to enter Mosul itself according to the military plan, while other forces secure surrounding areas.

1226553_1226553.caption: Hubei province Honghu city A fisherman rides a motor tricycle to transport dead fish killed by drought at his fish farm at Honghu lake
1226553_1226553.article_context: Central and southern China are experiencing a severe drought that has drastically lowered water levels in major rivers and reservoirs, including the Yangtze. The drought has led to widespread water shortages affecting millions of residents, devastated farmland, and caused significant losses in fisheries. Hydroelectric power generation has dropped, resulting in energy shortages and power cuts for factories and homes. Authorities are taking emergency measures such as water transfers and cloud seeding, but conditions remain critical as key waterways reach record low levels.

848019_848019.caption: Hunting and selling ortolans has been illegal in France since 1999 But some restaurants serve them at a cost of 150
848019_848019.article_context: Animal rights activists in France are intensifying their campaign against the illegal hunting and consumption of ortolans, endangered songbirds long considered a culinary delicacy. Members of the League for the Protection of Birds recently staged a protest, destroying traps and freeing captured birds, criticizing the government's ongoing failure to enforce existing bans. Despite laws prohibiting ortolan hunting since 1999, up to 50,000 birds are still poached annually, and some restaurants covertly serve them for high prices. The activists argue that protecting biodiversity must take precedence over controversial gastronomic traditions.

442338_442338.caption: Raul Castro s decision to let people enter the property market means that Cuban socialism is going to look quite different
442338_442338.article_context: The Cuban government has announced major reforms allowing citizens to legally buy and sell property for the first time since the 1959 revolution, ending decades of strict state control over housing. This change, initiated by President Raúl Castro, is part of broader moves to open up the economy, encourage private enterprise, and reduce the state's role. The new law creates a legal property market with some restrictions, and is expected to generate wealth for many Cubans, stimulate economic activity, and increase tax revenue. These reforms mark the most significant loosening of socialist policies since Fidel Castro's rule, though many challenges remain, such as the ongoing housing shortage and limitations for those without property.

422018_422018.caption: A Bangladeshi rescue worker walks at the site where a garmentfactory building collapsed on April 24 in Savar near Dhaka
422018_422018.article_context: Thousands of mourners gathered at the site of Bangladesh's Rana Plaza garment factory collapse to pray for the 1,127 victims, marking the end of a weeks-long recovery effort. The disaster, the deadliest in global garment industry history, prompted several major Western retailers—including H&M, Primark, Tesco, C&A, and Inditex—to agree to fund rigorous safety inspections and repairs in Bangladeshi factories. The Bangladeshi government responded by easing restrictions on union formation and establishing a new wage board, aiming to improve conditions in an industry notorious for low wages and poor safety. Nonetheless, some companies like Wal-Mart and Gap remain reluctant to join the safety pact, while labor activists stress the urgent need to end deadly factory disasters.

286169_286169.caption: Sen Bernie Sanders and Hillary Clinton participate in the PBS NewsHour Democratic presidential candidate debate
286169_286169.article_context: This weekend, primaries and caucuses will take place in five states, with Donald Trump and Hillary Clinton looking to solidify their positions as party front-runners. The Democratic candidates, Clinton and Bernie Sanders, are set to debate in Flint, Michigan, highlighting the city’s ongoing water crisis. Additionally, the College Board is introducing a redesigned SAT exam intended to better reflect college-level skills. In Gettysburg, a group will hold the first Confederate Flag Day, sparking renewed discussions around the flag’s meaning and history. Finally, the popular British series Downton Abbey will conclude its run with a two-hour finale on PBS.

657331_657331.caption: The Scottish parliament will be able to set income tax rates that could be 10 pence lower than the rest of the UK
657331_657331.article_context: Alex Salmond's Scottish government has agreed to accept major new financial powers, including the authority to set a distinct Scottish rate of income tax and control over certain property and environmental taxes, as part of an amended Scotland bill. In exchange, Salmond dropped his demands for full control over corporation tax and excise duty but secured increased borrowing powers for Scotland. These changes, described as the largest transfer of financial authority since 1707, will enable Scotland from 2016 to set its own tax rates and manage specific revenues independently, while the UK will reduce Scotland's block grant accordingly. This move comes as Salmond prepares for a 2014 independence referendum, but he faces pressure to clarify how the new fiscal powers will be used.

1041980_1041980.caption: Protests against fracking for shale in London Antifracking parliamentarians in Europe have won a symbolic vote against fracking
1041980_1041980.article_context: A majority of Members of the European Parliament (MEPs) supported a symbolic moratorium on fracking for shale gas, marking the first such backing but with no immediate legal effect. Although the related report was not adopted, the close vote highlighted growing political opposition to shale gas and is expected to prompt further debates and possible future legislative action at the EU level. This development reflects increasing uncertainty for both the European Commission and the shale industry, amid declining public support and ongoing arguments about environmental safety. Meanwhile, industry groups maintain that fracking is already proven safe, and political divisions persist over Europe's broader energy policy.

285638_285638.caption: Adele speaks after receiving a Grammy award in Los Angeles in February 2012
285638_285638.article_context: Adele's newest single 'Hello' has debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, breaking the record for the most downloads in a single week with 1.1 million. The song marks her fourth No. 1 hit and is the first ever to surpass one million weekly downloads. 'Hello' has also achieved massive popularity online, with over 196 million YouTube views and topping the global Spotify chart. Adele's upcoming album, '25,' is scheduled for release on November 20.

147837_147837.caption: Supporters of opposition leader Henrique Capriles protest in Caracas
147837_147837.article_context: Following Venezuela's closely contested presidential election, the country has become deeply polarized, with Nicolas Maduro declared the winner by a narrow margin over opposition leader Henrique Capriles. The result has triggered widespread protests, violent clashes, and a political crisis, with both sides blaming each other for the unrest. Capriles rejected the outcome and called Maduro 'illegitimate,' while Maduro has banned protests and refused a recount. The divisions have spilled into daily life, affecting families, communities, and even businesses, underscoring a heightened atmosphere of tension and hostility throughout Venezuela.

1638222_1638222.caption: India s ISRO has become the sixth space agency in the world to use an indigenous cryogenic engine to launch heavy satellites
1638222_1638222.article_context: India has joined an elite group of nations—alongside the US, Russia, France, Japan, China, and the European Space Agency—after the successful launch of its Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV-D5) using an indigenous cryogenic engine. This achievement follows years of setbacks and signifies India's newfound capability to launch heavier satellites into orbit. Separately, India and Pakistan have reactivated 16 border communication lines to reduce tensions, and Bangladesh and Afghanistan have sought India's expertise in eradicating polio after India's own success. In Punjab, villagers protested property taxes due to lack of development.

1507845_1507845.caption: Baby Yudier Moreno was held by a rescuer on the flight back to Quibdo
1507845_1507845.article_context: A young mother, Maria Nelly Murillo, and her one-year-old son were found alive five days after their small plane crashed in the jungle of western Colombia. The rescue, described as 'a miracle' by Colombian officials, occurred near the crash site in Choco province, where the pilot was found dead. Murillo and her son survived by using coconuts and rainwater before being located by search teams and airlifted to a hospital. The cause of the crash remains unknown.

110739_110739.caption: A German crowd gives the Nazi salute to the US Olympic contingent as it marches past the reviewing stand of Olympics host Adolf Hitler pictured in semisilhouette on the right
110739_110739.article_context: The term 'Lügenpresse', historically linked to Nazi propaganda and anti-democratic rhetoric in Germany, was recently shouted by Trump supporters at a rally, raising concerns due to its roots in hatred against journalists and minorities. The word, now a taboo in Germany, has been revived by right-wing, xenophobic groups and is associated with declining trust in mainstream media, leading to verbal and physical attacks on journalists. Originally coined in World War I as a reference to enemy propaganda, 'Lügenpresse' became an incendiary tool during the Nazi era, contributing to the persecution and deaths of millions. Its resurgence in political discourse underscores worries about the dangerous implications of using historically loaded language.

248819_248819.caption: A lava flow from Kilauea Volcano on the island of Hawaii crosses a road near Pahoa
248819_248819.article_context: Residents near Hawaii's Kilauea volcano prepared to evacuate as a fast-moving lava flow, reaching temperatures of 2,000 degrees Fahrenheit, neared homes on the outskirts of Pahoa. The lava, which had accelerated as it approached steeper ground, threatened 40 to 50 homes and businesses, prompting most residents to leave or ready themselves for evacuation, though no mandatory orders had been issued. Officials expressed concern that if the lava crossed Highway 130, it could isolate the Puna District from the rest of the island. Governor Neil Abercrombie requested federal disaster assistance, citing the risk of severe disruption and destruction if the town was cut off or damaged.

372186_372186.caption: Utility workers and investigators stand outside destroyed homes on Fieldfare Way in the Richmond Hills subdivision Monday
372186_372186.article_context: Investigators in Indianapolis are examining the cause of a deadly house explosion that killed two people and destroyed multiple homes, with evidence suggesting natural gas may have been involved. While the homeowner's daughter reported smelling an unusual odor in the weeks leading up to the blast, no leaks have been found in the neighborhood’s main gas lines or pipes. The investigation is complicated by extensive damage, making it difficult to pinpoint the exact source, and experts acknowledge the possibility that the precise cause may never be determined. Disputes have emerged between the homeowner’s attorney and the local utility company over accountability for the explosion.

164948_164948.caption: Small parachutes bearing food supplies for US Marines are dropped from a plane outside Forward Operating Base Edi in southern Afghanistan s Helmand province
164948_164948.article_context: A Senate Foreign Relations Committee report concludes that the U.S. nation-building efforts in Afghanistan have produced only limited success and may not be sustainable after American withdrawal. The report highlights major problems, including overwhelming aid spending, corruption, short-term fixes, and the creation of a dependent wartime economy that the Afghan government cannot sustain. It calls for a thorough rethinking of aid programs, better oversight, and an end to inflated salaries and projects that Afghans cannot maintain. With U.S. troop withdrawal plans underway, the report urges that future assistance focus on achievable, necessary, and sustainable development rather than rapid spending for short-term gains.

1672399_1672399.caption: ProRussian rebels control large parts of eastern Ukraine
1672399_1672399.article_context: The US has accused Russia of violating the Minsk ceasefire agreement by deploying additional air defence systems and increasing troop presence in eastern Ukraine. The State Department claims Russia is training separatist forces and building up its military along the border, marking the largest presence since October 2014. These actions allegedly breach the truce brokered in February, while Russia denies direct involvement. Despite the agreement, clashes have continued, and the conflict has resulted in over 6,000 deaths since its onset.

464425_464425.caption: Starchild a selfdescribed fulltime activist and libertarian holds a sign outside the flagship Apple store in San Francisco in support of the company
464425_464425.article_context: The FBI asked Apple to help unlock an iPhone used by one of the San Bernardino shooters, but Apple refused, citing security and privacy risks. A federal judge then ordered Apple to assist, intensifying a legal clash over whether national security can require technology companies to create hacking tools. Apple argues that creating such software would set a dangerous precedent, undermining digital privacy and affecting the security of all iPhones. The government claims its request is limited to this case, but the outcome could have far-reaching implications for encryption, technology law, and global privacy standards. The dispute is expected to continue in the courts, and has sparked debates across government, tech, and civil society.

343265_343265.caption: Donald Trump greets his supporters as he arrives to speak in New York on May 3 2016 following the primary in Indiana
343265_343265.article_context: Donald Trump secured the Republican presidential nomination after a convincing victory in the Indiana primary, leading both remaining rivals, Ted Cruz and John Kasich, to drop out. Despite skepticism within the GOP about Trump’s chances in the general election due to his lack of political experience and high unfavorable ratings, especially among key voter groups, the article examines his possible path to victory. Winning the presidency would require Trump to hold traditional Republican states and flip crucial battlegrounds like Florida, Ohio, and Pennsylvania, where polls currently favor his opponent, Hillary Clinton. His campaign faces significant challenges, but the unpredictability of the 2016 race leaves the outcome uncertain.

1601682_1601682.caption: France says 130 people died in last week s attacks on a number of sites including this cafe in Paris
1601682_1601682.article_context: The UN Security Council unanimously adopted a French-proposed resolution calling for intensified and coordinated international action against Islamic State (IS) following the deadly Paris attacks that killed 130 people. The resolution urges UN members to take all necessary measures to fight IS and condemns recent attacks in France, Lebanon, Tunisia, and Turkey attributed to the group. The move comes as Belgium raised Brussels’ terror alert to the highest level and continued investigations into the attacks. The resolution falls short of explicitly authorizing force but reflects growing international resolve, especially from France and Russia, to confront IS, which claimed responsibility for multiple recent terror attacks.

564327_564327.caption: Petro Poroshenko Today we can definitely say all of Ukraine has voted this is a national vote
564327_564327.article_context: Petro Poroshenko won Ukraine's presidential election with 56% of the vote, avoiding a runoff and beating rival Yulia Tymoshenko by a large margin. The election was seen as crucial for Ukraine’s future, with high voter turnout across most of the country, though many in the eastern regions were unable or unwilling to participate due to separatist activity and intimidation by pro-Russian groups. Poroshenko pledged to focus on ending the conflict in the east, unite the country, hold early parliamentary elections, improve relations with Russia, and pursue closer ties with the European Union. Despite international support, especially from the US and Germany, significant challenges remain due to ongoing unrest in the east and economic difficulties.

1581934_1581934.caption: Wildfires caused by illegal land clearing in Indonesias Sumatra and Borneo islands often spread choking haze to neighbouring countries Singapore and Malaysia
1581934_1581934.article_context: Indonesia continues to struggle with recurring forest fires and the resulting haze, which have caused widespread health issues, flight cancellations, and agricultural damage across the region for 18 years. Under increasing pressure, Indonesian authorities have named additional companies, including those from Malaysia, China, and Singapore, as suspects in starting the fires. President Joko Widodo, previously resistant to international aid, has now accepted regional assistance. However, activists criticize the lack of enforcement, as few legal actions have been taken against accused companies. Scientists warn that this year’s haze may be the worst since 1997, with potential economic losses estimated to exceed previous crises.

1586260_1586260.caption: Over 5000 people have died in violent attacks in Iraq since January the UN says
1586260_1586260.article_context: A brutal attack on two Shia Muslim family homes near Baghdad left at least 16 people dead, highlighting a surge in sectarian violence in Iraq. The assault is among several recent deadly incidents, including bombings that killed soldiers and police. This wave of violence has reached its highest level since 2008 and is fueled by growing sectarian tensions, political unrest, and spillover from the Syrian conflict. Despite government crackdowns on militant groups, attacks continue to target both security forces and civilians, with over 5,000 killed since January.

1255743_1255743.caption: Occupy Wall Street protesters gather in Washington Square Park New York
1255743_1255743.article_context: Inspired by the Occupy Wall Street movement, activists in the UK are planning to 'occupy' the London Stock Exchange this weekend as part of a global day of action against the financial industry. The protest, organised via social media, reflects widespread discontent over bank bailouts, economic inequality, and lack of political representation, and is part of over 800 similar events worldwide. In London, protesters intend to gather at St Paul's Cathedral before marching to the Stock Exchange, though there are uncertainties over police response and the ability to set up long-term camps. The movement, endorsed by prominent figures and inspired by the Arab Spring, calls for democratization of global finance. While some financial leaders have expressed willingness to engage in dialogue, there has been little response from UK banks so far.

679750_679750.caption: Republican Governor Tom Corbett speaks during a gubernatorial debate with Democrat Tom Wolf
679750_679750.article_context: A scandal involving the exchange of pornographic emails by current and former Pennsylvania attorney general’s office staff has led to the resignation of two top officials in Governor Tom Corbett’s administration: Environmental Protection Secretary Christopher Abruzzo and lawyer Glenn Parno. The controversy, which also implicates other officials including state police commissioner Frank Noonan, is putting pressure on Corbett as he seeks re-election. The investigation began after Attorney General Kathleen Kane reviewed emails discovered during the Jerry Sandusky case, revealing hundreds of inappropriate messages among staff who worked under Corbett when he was attorney general. The scandal has prompted calls for further inquiries into whether judges were involved and raised questions about Corbett’s office management.

409541_409541.caption: Trump arrives at the airport for a visit to the USMexico border in Laredo Texas on July 23 2015
409541_409541.article_context: Donald Trump advocated for the revival of stop-and-frisk policing to address inner-city violence during a Fox News interview, referencing its prior use in New York City under Mayor Rudy Giuliani. Critics argue the practice leads to racial profiling and disproportionately targets minorities, a concern validated by a U.S. District Court ruling against New York’s program. Trump’s remarks followed recent fatal police shootings involving African Americans and the resulting nationwide protests, amid ongoing debates on the effectiveness and fairness of stop-and-frisk.

1003100_1003100.caption: XCOM 2 s missions offer an authentic edge of risk
1003100_1003100.article_context: XCOM 2, the sequel to Firaxis’ acclaimed strategy game, begins twenty years after humanity’s defeat by aliens in the original, thrusting players into a guerrilla resistance against the ruling alien-human Advent regime. The gameplay combines turn-based tactical missions with resource-scarce base management, emphasizing tough decisions and meaningful consequences. New mechanics increase urgency and pacing, including frequent turn-limited objectives and a doomsday clock. While technical issues persist with multi-level building navigation, XCOM 2 is lauded for refining the series’ core strategy, enhancing both challenge and player satisfaction.

818054_818054.caption: A baby girl is carried to safety by Pakistani navy personnel in the village of Panu Akil near Sukkur in the heartland province of Sindh
818054_818054.article_context: Floods in southern Pakistan have affected 12 million people and destroyed 650,000 homes, with authorities warning that more villages are at risk as monsoon rains persist. The crisis, described as the worst flooding in 80 years, has led to mass evacuations in Sindh province and extensive damage to agricultural lands, threatening a food crisis. Over 1,600 people have reportedly died, and relief efforts are hampered by damaged infrastructure, while criticism grows over President Zardari's absence. International aid, including £10 million from Britain, is being mobilized, but Pakistani authorities continue to struggle with providing basic necessities and preventing disease outbreaks among the displaced population.

1198905_1198905.caption: Scottish Labour leader Jim Murphy has accused Nicola Sturgeon s SNP of using the general election to stoke up discontent and division
1198905_1198905.article_context: Scottish Labour leader Jim Murphy accused the SNP, led by Nicola Sturgeon, of seeking to divide Scotland by pushing for a second independence referendum after new polls showed a significant rise in SNP support. Sturgeon, meanwhile, criticized Labour and the Conservatives for refusing to embrace a multi-party election and reiterated the SNP's willingness to work with other parties to keep the Conservatives out of power, while denying immediate plans for another referendum. Labour leadership, supported by Ed Balls, insisted there would be no deals with the SNP, arguing their demands were fundamentally incompatible and warning their economic plans would result in greater austerity. The debate highlights deepening divisions over Scotland's future, the SNP's intentions regarding independence, and the parties' willingness to cooperate following the general election.

1570438_1570438.caption: Flying Officer Marium Mukhtiar s body was transported to Karachi
1570438_1570438.article_context: Flying Officer Marium Mukhtiar, the first Pakistani female fighter pilot to die in operational service, was laid to rest in Karachi after a fatal training flight accident in Punjab. Mukhtiar and her co-pilot ejected from their aircraft following an in-flight emergency, but she later died from her injuries while the co-pilot survived. Her death was widely mourned and praised as a major loss and a moment of national pride, reflecting her role as a pioneer for women in Pakistan's Air Force, which began admitting women into combat roles in 2006. The cause of the crash remains under investigation, and it follows a series of recent military aviation accidents in Pakistan.

193029_193029.caption: How Obama s commencement speech took on Trump without mentioning his name
193029_193029.article_context: In a commencement speech at Rutgers University, President Obama strongly criticized Donald Trump’s proposals and rhetoric without mentioning him by name. Obama denounced Trump’s plan to build a border wall, the call to 'Make America Great Again,' and the broader trend of anti-intellectualism and rejection of facts in politics. He urged graduates to value experience, critical thinking, and compromise in democratic life, emphasizing optimism about America’s future and encouraging continued civic engagement and faith in democracy.

46686_46686.caption: A tobacco deal got Gov Chris Christie 92 million for his budget but rating agencies downgraded New Jersey s credit anyway for its reliance on onetime fiscal fixes
46686_46686.article_context: After the 1998 tobacco settlement, which required tobacco companies to pay states over $200 billion to address smoking-related health costs, many states and local governments turned to Wall Street for upfront cash by selling bonds backed by future tobacco payments. Wall Street created complex and risky financial instruments called capital appreciation bonds (CABs), promising huge payments decades later. These deals raised billions for states quickly, but relied on overly optimistic predictions about cigarette sales, resulting in declining revenues and massive balloon debts. Today, states are facing fiscal burdens, defaults are likely, and taxpayers are indirectly affected as money meant for public health programs is funneled to pay off Wall Street investors. Investment banks and consultants made over $500 million in fees, while states struggle to refinance, bail out, or renegotiate toxic deals linked to shrinking tobacco money. Critics argue these arrangements diverted settlement funds away from their intended purpose of smoking prevention and health care.

1449521_1449521.caption: AQIM released pictures of Mr Verdon with fellow captive Serge Lazarevic
1449521_1449521.article_context: Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb claimed to have executed French national Philippe Verdon, who was kidnapped in Mali in 2011, as retaliation for France's military intervention against Islamist militants in Mali. France began its campaign in January to stop militants from overrunning the capital, and has since recaptured major cities previously under Islamist control. The report of Verdon's death is yet to be officially confirmed by the French government. Fourteen French nationals remain hostages in Africa, with six believed to be held in Mali. France plans to withdraw its 4,000 troops next month, transitioning security responsibilities to West African forces ahead of scheduled elections.

1243824_1243824.caption: Emergency service workers take away activists from the pressure group Plane Stupid who occupied the north runway at Heathrow on Monday
1243824_1243824.article_context: Residents of the historic village of Harmondsworth, which faces partial demolition due to plans for a third runway at Heathrow Airport, have escalated their opposition through civil disobedience and direct action. Thirteen protesters from the group Plane Stupid cut through Heathrow’s perimeter fence and occupied a runway, resulting in flight cancellations and their arrest. Both longtime villagers and outside activists cite the destruction of homes and the environmental impact, particularly climate change, as central concerns, with some residents expressing willingness to continue such actions as the government prepares to make a final decision on the expansion by year’s end.

41206_41206.caption: People wait for Nicola Sturgeon the leader of the Scottish National Party to make a speech in Edinburgh
41206_41206.article_context: As immigration emerges as a central and contentious issue in Britain's general election campaign, many immigrants say they are being unfairly blamed for society’s problems by politicians seeking to tighten border controls. In response, a crowdfunded 'I am an immigrant' poster campaign has appeared nationwide, highlighting immigrants' positive contributions to British society. Politicians across the spectrum have adopted tough stances on immigration, with parties like UKIP making anti-immigration rhetoric a key issue, while the Conservative and Labour leaders promise reforms and tighter controls. However, with millions of immigrants eligible to vote, the political debate is complicated by the need to either court or risk alienating this diverse and significant voting bloc.

39941_39941.caption: In Izhevsk Russia residents of a complex of buildings on Kommunarov Street one day woke up to workmen tearing up their courtyard The residents are unhappy they were nt consulted say they have no use for such a wide road and suspect it is being built as an opportunity for personal profit
39941_39941.article_context: As regional elections approach in Russia, President Vladimir Putin and his United Russia party are consolidating their top-down control, especially in rural areas like Izhevsk in the Udmurt Republic. Local officials tie government benefits, such as playgrounds or funding, to community support for United Russia, pressuring residents to back the party. Opposition candidates face intimidation and removal from ballots, making challenges to the system difficult. Projects like a $500,000 courtyard renovation are seen by locals as driven more by bureaucratic self-interest and opportunities for profit than public need. Despite the presence of some opposition, most residents feel powerless to influence government decisions, which are tightly linked to loyalty to Putin and his party.

40824_40824.caption: Huckabee seen here in Dallas said he would wait until a rival got the 1191 delegates needed to win the nomination before stepping aside On March 4 McCain received the necessary delegates after winning in Texas Ohio Rhode Island and Vermont Huckabee conceded
40824_40824.article_context: Former Arkansas governor Mike Huckabee announced his candidacy for the 2016 Republican presidential nomination at a rally in his hometown of Hope, Arkansas. Huckabee, known for winning the 2008 Iowa caucuses and his appeal to evangelical voters, faces significant challenges in a crowded field of well-financed contenders. His political career includes serving as Arkansas governor and lieutenant governor, where he achieved notable legislative accomplishments despite opposition. Huckabee’s campaign will emphasize his Arkansas roots and his longstanding political connection to the Clinton family.

40790_40790.caption: Sen Bernie Sanders held court in Iowa earlier this month
40790_40790.article_context: The article argues that Democrats should not fear Bernie Sanders's calls for political revolution, as the party's most significant achievements have roots in past revolutionary movements. Historically, radical ideas—such as those from the Populists, the New Deal, the New Left, and civil rights activists—were initially seen as fringe but eventually became central to the Democratic platform and broader American society. The piece emphasizes that revolutionary ideas have repeatedly shaped and renewed the party, urging Democrats to recognize that bold proposals from the left have functioned as catalysts for important reforms rather than threats to stability. It concludes that revolutionary and pragmatic approaches are complementary forces within the party, and Sanders’s rhetoric continues a tradition of political imagination that drives progress.

40648_40648.caption: Turkish riot police rest at Taksim Square in Istanbul
40648_40648.article_context: Mass protests erupted across Turkey in response to a harsh police crackdown on a peaceful environmental demonstration in Istanbul, quickly expanding into nationwide anti-government demonstrations against Prime Minister Recep Tayyip Erdogan. Protesters cite a variety of grievances, including concerns over eroding personal freedoms, religious conservatism, government policies toward Syria, and longstanding regional tensions. Erdogan, who still retains strong support among conservative voters, has denounced the demonstrators as 'anarchists and terrorists,' raising fears of direct confrontation. Despite the diversity of issues fueling the unrest, the protests have united many young, educated Turks concerned with the government's direction and its effects on democracy and individual rights.

40710_40710.caption: A vendor pushes past heaps of garbage in downtown PortAuPrince on June 10 The area is home to a busy marketplace that was once occupied by brickandmortar businesses that were not rebuilt after the earthquake in 2010
40710_40710.article_context: Haiti is experiencing a deep political crisis after last year’s disputed presidential election was annulled due to fraud allegations, leaving the country without a stable government. The interim president, Jocelerme Privert, has overstayed his 120-day mandate, but parliament has not extended his term or agreed on a replacement, leading to uncertainty and political deadlock. This crisis compounds Haiti's ongoing challenges, including economic hardship, disease, and widespread poverty, while foreign donors and governments grow increasingly frustrated with Haiti’s inability to achieve political stability. New elections are tentatively planned for October, but there is little confidence that they will resolve the systemic problems undermining Haitian democracy.

40188_40188.caption: Cruz disagrees with Trump s Muslim ban but wo nt criticize him
40188_40188.article_context: While Donald Trump leads national polls in the 2016 Republican presidential race, Ted Cruz is emerging as the strongest contender for the nomination. Cruz's appeal to very conservative voters, significant fundraising success, rising momentum as the Iowa caucuses front-runner, and favorable primary calendar positioning give him a clear path to securing the nomination. Although Cruz faces challenges in broadening his appeal beyond core conservatives, his timing and strategic strengths suggest he is well-positioned to be the 'last man standing' in the race.

41406_41406.caption: Lynch defends the Obama administration s actions on issues from immigration to surveillance during her hearing
41406_41406.article_context: Loretta Lynch was confirmed by the U.S. Senate as attorney general, ending a five-month delay since her nomination by President Obama. She becomes the first African American woman to hold the position, succeeding Eric Holder. The confirmation process was marked by intense partisan debate, particularly over her support for Obama's immigration policies and an unrelated dispute over abortion funding in an anti-trafficking bill. Despite the opposition of many Republicans, ten crossed party lines to support her in a 56-43 vote. Lynch is expected to be sworn in as the nation's 83rd attorney general.

40674_40674.caption: Trump Mitt Romney let us down
40674_40674.article_context: In New Hampshire, Donald Trump is outperforming Jeb Bush in the Republican presidential primary race, drawing larger crowds and leading recent polls. Trump has galvanized voters with his anti-establishment rhetoric and sharp attacks on Bush, while Bush has struggled to energize his campaign and is being challenged by other establishment candidates, notably Ohio Gov. John Kasich, who is gaining endorsements and rising in the polls. The Republican field remains crowded and divided, with traditional candidates competing against political outsiders, and Bush facing difficulty consolidating mainstream support as attention shifts toward fresh faces like Kasich.

39730_39730.caption: Sarah Silverman an early Bernie Sanders backer implored people to vote for Clinton When Sanders supporters objected she quipped To the Bernieorbust people let me just tell you You re being ridiculous
39730_39730.article_context: A new Washington Post-ABC News poll shows that Donald Trump failed to gain voter support from the Republican National Convention in 2016, with more people saying the event made them less likely to back him. In contrast, Hillary Clinton's favorability and enthusiastic support improved significantly after the Democratic convention, especially among independents and former Bernie Sanders supporters. The Republican convention did not unify the party around Trump, while the Democratic convention helped solidify Clinton’s base and attract moderate Republicans, emphasizing the effectiveness of the Democrats’ outreach and the shortcomings of Trump’s convention.

40747_40747.caption: Trump says he would rather run against Hillary Clinton
40747_40747.article_context: A new Quinnipiac University poll suggests Donald Trump is likely to secure the Republican presidential nomination, maintaining a strong lead over opponents even if rivals Ted Cruz or John Kasich drop out. However, the same poll indicates that Trump is currently less popular than Hillary Clinton in a general election matchup, with Clinton holding a six-point lead and Trump facing high levels of opposition from Republicans and independents alike. The findings highlight Trump's strength within the Republican base but raise doubts about his ability to win broader support in the general election.

39502_39502.caption: Sen Bernie Sanders former secretary of state Hillary Clinton and former Maryland governor Martin OMalley arrive onstage for the second Democratic National Committee presidential primary debate at Drake University in Des Moines Iowa on Nov 14 The DNC has suspended its partnership with WMURTV for the third debate on Dec 19
39502_39502.article_context: The Democratic National Committee (DNC) has dropped local TV station WMUR as a co-sponsor for an upcoming presidential debate in New Hampshire due to an ongoing contract dispute between WMUR’s parent company, Hearst Corp., and its unionized production workers. The DNC cited its commitment to supporting union rights as the reason for the decision, emphasizing that not supporting union labor could risk alienating a key party constituency. While the move aligns with the party’s labor principles and may appease union supporters, it also raises concerns about the party’s tolerance for disagreement and could reinforce criticism about ideological exclusivity.

40436_40436.caption: Blatter I can not monitor everyone all the time
40436_40436.article_context: FIFA President Sepp Blatter publicly responded to the ongoing FBI investigation into widespread corruption within FIFA, distancing himself from allegations and asserting he cannot be held responsible for the actions of others. His comments came after several current and former FIFA officials, as well as business executives, were indicted on charges including racketeering and wire fraud. FIFA’s ethics committee immediately banned 11 individuals linked to the scandal. Despite growing criticism and calls to postpone the presidential election, Blatter remains the frontrunner for a fifth term, promising FIFA’s cooperation with investigators and acknowledging the organization's severe loss of trust.

40914_40914.caption: With his wife Evelyn by his side Chicago mayoral candidate Jesus Chuy Garcia speaks to the press after casting his ballot on election day Feb 24 2015 in Chicago Garcia will face Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel in a runoff election in April
40914_40914.article_context: Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel failed to win an outright majority in his re-election bid, forcing him into a runoff against liberal challenger Jesus 'Chuy' Garcia. Emanuel received 46 percent of the vote, while Garcia secured 34 percent, setting up a decisive election on April 7. The close race highlights divisions within the Democratic Party, with Garcia backed by progressive activists and the teachers union, and Emanuel supported by President Obama and other establishment figures. The runoff marks the first such contest since Chicago's election laws changed in 1995, posing challenges for Garcia to gain resources to compete with Emanuel, who has heavily outspent his opponents.

40807_40807.caption: Standoff snags impeachment process against Brazil s president
40807_40807.article_context: Brazil’s Senate prepared to vote on impeaching President Dilma Rousseff, a decision that would suspend her from office and put her on trial for allegedly breaking budget laws. The move follows months of political turmoil, economic crisis, and corruption scandals. Rousseff, whose popularity has plummeted, faces accusations of manipulating government accounts to conceal the state of Brazil’s finances, though she denies wrongdoing. If impeached by a simple Senate majority, Vice President Michel Temer would become interim president while the Senate holds a final trial. Rousseff and her supporters label the process a ‘coup,’ but most lawmakers and observers expect her removal.

39299_39299.caption: Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell of Ky joined by his wife former Labor Secretary Elaine Chao celebrates with his supporters at an election night party in Louisville Ky Tuesday Nov 4 2014
39299_39299.article_context: In the battle for the 2014 Senate, Republicans executed a disciplined campaign strategy focused on tying Democratic incumbents to President Obama's unpopular policies and avoiding candidate missteps, while Democrats struggled with internal divisions and waning White House support. GOP leaders intervened in troubled campaigns, recruited strong candidates, and improved digital and ground operations, helping them recover from past failures and unseat vulnerable Democrats. Democrats tried to localize races and boost turnout among their core voters, but challenges arising from Obama's low approval rating and several administrative controversies hurt their efforts. Notable events included dramatic campaign shake-ups, tough primaries against hardline conservatives, and a relentless campaign in states like Kansas, where Republicans salvaged Senator Pat Roberts’s campaign to keep their Senate majority. Ultimately, the Republican Party's tighter coordination, candidate discipline, and effective messaging led to significant wins and a shift in Senate control.

41263_41263.caption: Michelle Obama has become Hillary Clinton s secret weapon
41263_41263.article_context: Michelle Obama has become a highly influential surrogate for Hillary Clinton during the 2016 presidential campaign, drawing large, enthusiastic crowds—especially young and African American voters. Renowned for her emotional, authentic speaking style, she energizes the electorate and contrasts herself with Hillary Clinton's more formal approach. Her speeches focus on framing Donald Trump as unfit for the presidency, often without naming him directly, while praising Clinton's character. Obama uniquely addresses concerns about voter enthusiasm and third-party candidates by urging Democrats to vote, emphasizing the importance of participation. Her role, seen as unifying and impactful, stands out for its personal touch and blunt messaging.

39802_39802.caption: View Photo Gallery The former US senator from Pennsylvania is seeking the Republican presidential nomination
39802_39802.article_context: Rick Santorum won the Kansas Republican caucuses, securing a significant lead over Mitt Romney and other candidates, which strengthens his standing as the leading social conservative in the GOP race. Santorum's victory comes as Romney and Newt Gingrich chose not to campaign in Kansas, focusing instead on other upcoming primaries. The win provides Santorum with momentum and a larger share of delegates, fueling arguments for a two-man contest between him and Romney for the Republican nomination.

39365_39365.caption: Morsi supporters gather outside the Republican Guard headquarters
39365_39365.article_context: After Egypt's military ousted President Mohamed Morsi, the country's first democratically elected leader, authorities installed an interim president, Adly Mansour, and ordered the arrests of senior Muslim Brotherhood members. The crackdown targeted prominent Brotherhood figures, with Morsi and several associates placed under house arrest and warrants issued for top leaders. The Brotherhood called for nationwide protests in response. The situation has raised concerns about possible further violence and repression, while the U.S. faces a diplomatic dilemma over its financial support and how to respond to the military-led transition. Millions of Egyptians had supported Morsi's removal due to dissatisfaction with his leadership, but the military's intervention signals continued uncertainty about the future of Egyptian democracy.

39399_39399.caption: Democrat Terry McAuliffe celebrates winning the Virginia governorship at an election night party at the Sheraton Premiere Hotel November 5 2013 in Tysons Corner Virginia McAuliffe defeated state Attorney General Ken Cuccinelli
39399_39399.article_context: Election Night 2013 saw major wins for Democrat Terry McAuliffe, who disciplined his campaign to focus on jobs, and Republican Chris Christie, who secured a broad coalition in his New Jersey re-election, boosting speculation about his 2016 presidential prospects. Moderates played a key role in deciding outcomes, especially in Virginia and New Jersey. Unions gained ground with union-friendly candidates winning mayoral races in New York City and Boston. Conversely, candidates who focused on social issues, like Ken Cuccinelli, suffered significant losses, revealing that moderates, rather than independents, are now the swing group. The results also highlighted the shrinking influence of white voters and public polling inaccuracies. Additionally, Michael Bloomberg's legacy was challenged by Bill de Blasio’s victory in New York, and there was growing voter concern about government overreach.

43851_43851.caption: A woman blows smoke rings with marijuana smoke during the 420 Rally at the Civic Center in Denver Colorado April 20 2014 REUTERSMark Leffingwell
43851_43851.article_context: The debate over marijuana policy in the U.S. has led to unusual political alliances, as support for decriminalization or legalization now spans both major parties. Public opinion has shifted significantly, with a majority supporting treatment over prosecution for minor offenses and increasing backing for legalization across the political spectrum. While only two states—Colorado and Washington—have fully legalized recreational marijuana, many others have moved towards decriminalization or approved medical use. Politicians from different backgrounds, such as Republicans Rand Paul, Rick Perry, and Tom Tancredo, and Democrats Martin O'Malley and Cory Booker, have endorsed reforms, citing concerns about justice, public health, and government overreach. The next key battles over legalization are expected in several states in 2016, signaling a potential nationwide shift in marijuana policy.

41671_41671.caption: Dolezal the president of the NAACP in Spokane Wash meets Joseph M King left and Scott Finnie at an event on public safety and criminal justice in Cheney Wash
41671_41671.article_context: Rachel Dolezal, the former NAACP leader who claimed a black identity despite being born white, has sparked controversy among transracial adoptees. Many adoptees and advocates criticize the use of 'transracial' to describe Dolezal, arguing it distorts and trivializes the real, lived experiences of those adopted into families of different racial backgrounds. In an open letter, they assert that Dolezal’s story is fundamentally different from the challenges faced by transracial adoptees, who navigate issues of identity, belonging, and racism from childhood. The debate highlights broader tensions in identity politics and concerns about misrepresenting complex social realities.

41412_41412.caption: President John F Kennedy meets with Soviet Foreign Minister Andrei Gromyko center at the White House on Oct 18 1962 At left is Anatoly Dobrynin the Soviet ambassador to the United States
41412_41412.article_context: Newly released archival documents from the 1962 Cuban missile crisis reveal that Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev did not support a nuclear first strike, a fact unknown to U.S. policymakers at the time and which led to a costly nuclear arms buildup based on flawed assumptions. The article draws parallels to current U.S. policy toward Iran, highlighting the importance of understanding an adversary's true intentions regarding nuclear weapons. Despite Iranian leaders' public statements that nuclear weapons are religiously prohibited, there remains uncertainty about their actual nuclear ambitions. The Cuban missile crisis serves as a reminder to seek accurate intelligence and employ cautious diplomacy to avoid unintended escalation, advocating the principle of 'trust but verify' when assessing security threats.

43768_43768.caption: Kerry Dollar could suffer if US abandons Iran deal
43768_43768.article_context: Three dozen retired U.S. generals and admirals released an open letter endorsing the Iran nuclear deal, calling it the most effective way to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons and urging Congress to support it. Their backing provided the White House with additional support amid intense congressional debate and opposition, as lawmakers prepared to vote on whether to disapprove the agreement. Secretary of State John Kerry warned that rejecting the deal would harm U.S. credibility and isolate America from its allies, while military leaders argued military action would be less effective than the agreement. The debate comes amid divided views among Democrats and strong opposition from the Israeli government and pro-Israel groups.

40752_40752.caption: Kim Jong Un inspects new military technology made by unit 1501 of the Korean People s Army in 2013
40752_40752.article_context: A U.S. cyberattack targeting North Korea's nuclear program failed largely because North Korea has extremely limited Internet access, with most citizens restricted to a state-controlled intranet. The lack of Internet infrastructure in the country made it nearly impossible for the U.S. malware to penetrate North Korean systems. This isolation serves as both a defensive measure against foreign cyberattacks and a secure base for North Korea’s own cyber operations, such as the activities of its hacking unit known as Bureau 121. Despite its limited Internet, North Korea has successfully launched cyberattacks against entities like South Korean banks and Sony Pictures.

43207_43207.caption: Pakistani rescuers move an injured victim outside Bacha Khan university after an attack by gunmen in Charsadda on Jan 20
43207_43207.article_context: Following a deadly attack on a university in Pakistan, scholar Shenila Khoja-Moolji analyzes why girls' education is often targeted by both extremist groups and global humanitarian campaigns. She explains that education for girls has long been used by both colonial powers and modern Western institutions to define populations as either civilized or backward, often portraying Muslim women as victims in need of rescue. This dynamic is still at play today, as seen in global advocacy efforts and the narrative around figures like Malala Yousafzai. Extremist groups attack girls' education to oppose what they see as Western or colonial influence, while Western interventions often reinforce binaries of superiority and inferiority. Khoja-Moolji argues for a more nuanced approach that includes local traditions and perspectives to make girls' education less of a flashpoint and more supportive of real progress.

42804_42804.caption: People walk on a road blanketed with stones to block traffic on the outskirts of La Paz Bolivia Hundreds of miners are blocking three principal highways leading into Bolivia s capital city demanding that authorities grant them rather than a rival group of miners control over a profitable tin mine
42804_42804.article_context: Russian President Vladimir Putin has expelled the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) from Russia, ending over two decades of U.S. assistance that supported democracy, human rights, health, and environmental programs. The decision is viewed as part of Putin's broader crackdown on non-governmental organizations receiving foreign funding, especially those promoting political reforms and civil society. The move will significantly impact Russian groups that relied on USAID support, and is expected to further strain U.S.-Russia relations. The expulsion follows new Russian laws restricting foreign-funded NGOs and reflects growing tensions between the two countries over issues such as election monitoring and democracy promotion.

41173_41173.caption: Colombia President Juan Manuel Santos smiles as he addresses reporters with his wife first lady Maria Clemencia de Santos after winning the Nobel Peace Prize at Narino Palace in Bogota on Oct 7
41173_41173.article_context: Colombian President Juan Manuel Santos was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for his efforts to negotiate a peace deal with FARC rebels, aiming to end the country's 52-year conflict. Despite international support and a signed agreement, Santos suffered a setback when Colombian voters narrowly rejected the deal in a referendum, leading to political turmoil and a challenge from his chief rival, former president Álvaro Uribe. The Nobel Prize has bolstered Santos's standing internationally, but the future of the peace process remains uncertain as opponents push for tougher terms and negotiations continue.

41192_41192.caption: A soldier from the Central African Republic stands guard at a building used for joint meetings between members of the Central African Republic s military and US Army Special Forces soldiers in the town of Obo
41192_41192.article_context: The joint Ugandan and U.S. military operation to capture Joseph Kony, leader of the Lord’s Resistance Army (LRA), has been suspended due to political upheaval in the Central African Republic, where Kony is believed to be hiding. Rebel groups recently took over the country, disrupting cooperation with foreign troops. Despite the pause, U.S. and Ugandan soldiers will remain in the region, but halt active tracking until stability returns. The U.S. also announced a $5 million reward for information leading to Kony or other top LRA leaders. The suspension has raised concerns among human rights groups that Kony and the LRA may exploit the situation to resume attacks and abductions, as the group's presence still threatens civilians in the area.

42226_42226.caption: Policemen and security personnel argue with journalists outside the Atlapa Convention Center
42226_42226.article_context: In a historic meeting during the Summit of the Americas, President Obama and Cuban President Raúl Castro publicly agreed to work toward normalizing relations after decades of official hostility between the U.S. and Cuba. Both leaders emphasized their willingness to discuss disagreements with mutual respect, with immediate goals including reopening embassies in Washington and Havana. While Castro praised Obama as honest and exempt from past U.S. actions against Cuba, he insisted Cuba would not accept changes to its political system. Obama expressed optimism about progress and reaffirmed the U.S. stance on human rights. The meeting marked a major step in ending longstanding tensions and was seen as a potential legacy achievement for Obama’s presidency.

43344_43344.caption: At a national meeting at the April 25 House of Culture North Koreans mark an anniversary of the Fatherland Liberation War in Pyongyang
43344_43344.article_context: North Korea conducted its third underground nuclear test, claiming it involved a 'miniaturized' device that could be used with a long-range missile, raising concerns about its capability to reach the United States. The test, which caused a 4.9-magnitude seismic event, was the first under leader Kim Jong Eun and comes amid ongoing tensions and threats from Pyongyang. The United Nations Security Council called an emergency meeting in response, while Japan and other nations urged strict international action. The test follows North Korea's recent long-range rocket launch and indicates progress in its nuclear weapons program, likely involving uranium enrichment technology.

40394_40394.caption: Attendees at the Morris Brown AME Church prayer vigil
40394_40394.article_context: After the mass shooting of nine black churchgoers in Charleston, President Obama publicly reflected on his presidency’s struggles with gun control and racial reconciliation. He described the inability to pass gun legislation after events like Newtown as his deepest frustration and lamented that U.S. politics has become gridlocked and polarized, preventing meaningful progress. On race, Obama acknowledged both the changing national conversation and the persistent challenges, citing his more open discussions on racial issues but noting that substantive advances have been modest. As Obama prepared to deliver a eulogy in Charleston, he admitted he had not been the unifying, transformational figure many hoped, highlighting how political divisions had limited achievements on guns and race during his tenure.

42110_42110.caption: Sen John Barrasso RWyo left is leading a group of 34 GOP senators demanding the State Department explain why Russia is launching airstrikes against Syria from Iran
42110_42110.article_context: Senate Republicans have called on the Obama administration to take stronger action against Russia for its recent airstrikes in Syria launched from an Iranian airbase, which they argue violate the U.N. Security Council resolution supporting the Iran nuclear deal. In a letter to Secretary of State John Kerry, nearly three dozen Republican senators questioned whether these strikes were permissible and urged the administration to enforce consequences if they were not. The lawmakers contend that the administration is failing to uphold the arms embargo and question both the Iran nuclear agreement and U.S. policy toward Russia in Syria. Although the Russian and Iranian governments said the use of the base was temporary, Republicans warn it could happen again and demand measures to deter further such actions.

40654_40654.caption: North Koreans walk in front of the Mansudae Assembly Hall in Pyongyang last week A rare parliamentary session closed Tuesday without the announcement of economic policy changes that many outside experts had predicted
40654_40654.article_context: North Korea concluded a rare parliamentary session without announcing any anticipated economic reforms, tempering expectations about policy changes under leader Kim Jong Eun. Despite outside speculation that reforms would allow farmers to keep and sell more of their crops, the meeting only produced minor personnel changes and an extension of compulsory education. Experts suggest that reforms may still occur quietly, without public acknowledgment, as North Korea is cautious about openly changing its tightly controlled system. The country continues to prioritize military spending over resolving food shortages, and its rationing system has largely broken down, forcing citizens to rely on illicit markets.

39819_39819.caption: Ben Carson and Candy Carson meet with NGO representatives at the children s facility at the Azraq Syrian refugee camp in Jordan
39819_39819.article_context: Republican presidential candidate Ben Carson made a surprise visit to two Syrian refugee camps in Jordan as part of a private 'fact-finding' trip, with no media present. During his visit, Carson met with refugees and aid workers and called for the U.S. to focus on supporting refugees in the Middle East instead of resettling them in America, arguing that Jordan already houses over a million Syrians and needs more international aid.
